relations.name: analytics.meta_ads
relations.purpose: Dimension: one row per Meta ad (every ad the pipeline has ever seen: 42K, most ARCHIVED or DELETED) with its campaign, ad set, product, status and all-time totals. Join to the daily views on ad_id (they already carry the main names).
relations.source: public.meta_ads + meta_campaigns + meta_family_map + the product rule below + meta_ad_lifetime
relations.refresh: nightly (etl service 13:00 UTC): ad names, campaigns and totals from the Meta Graph API, status refreshed every night
relations.coverage: every ad with delivery since 2026-05-06 plus every ad the all-time pull returned; first_day / last_day only for ads that delivered since 2026-05-06
caveats: product_slug follows the Products table: a Meta family that maps to a tracker family counts under the product of that family's FIRST tracker row; a family off the tracker keeps the product guessed from its name, then campaign, then ad set; NULL = no active product. About 12K Meta families are on no tracker row.
family_key is the lower-cased ad name with ' - Copy N' and merge-tag suffixes stripped: copies of one ad share a family.

lifetime_* are Meta-reported all-time totals through the last complete day (Graph insights, both accounts, replaced nightly). They cover the whole life of the ad, not just 2026-05-06 onward; the daily views start on 2026-05-06.
status is Meta's effective_status; CAMPAIGN_PAUSED and ADSET_PAUSED mean the ad itself is on but a parent is off.

columns.name: ad_id
columns.description: Meta ad id (text, as Meta returns it).

columns.name: account
columns.description: Ad account name: 'Lonvera Main' (America/Los_Angeles) or 'Lonvera BackUp' (America/New_York).

columns.name: ad_name
columns.description: Current ad name in Meta (renames move the whole history).

columns.name: family_name
columns.description: Ad name without ' - Copy N' / merge-tag suffixes, original case: the ad family.

columns.name: family_key
columns.description: Lower-cased family_name. The join key to the creative tracker side (meta_family_map).

columns.name: tracker_family_key
columns.description: Creative-tracker family this Meta family was matched to by the resolver (NULL = no tracker row). Joins creative_tracker.family_key.

columns.name: product_slug
columns.description: vita-bull | beef-liver | boneflex | vita-belle | vital-flow | unassigned, by the rule in the view description; NULL = no active product.

columns.name: campaign_name
columns.description: Campaign name. A name containing 'test' makes the campaign a testing campaign.

columns.name: stage
columns.description: 'testing' when the campaign name contains 'test' (case-insensitive), else 'scaling'. A naming rule, not a Meta field.

columns.name: status
columns.description: Meta effective_status: ACTIVE, PAUSED, CAMPAIGN_PAUSED, ADSET_PAUSED, ARCHIVED, DELETED, DISAPPROVED, WITH_ISSUES.

columns.name: is_active
columns.description: status = 'ACTIVE' (the ad is eligible to deliver; it may still have spent nothing yet).

columns.name: created_date
columns.description: Pacific calendar date the ad was created.

columns.name: first_day
columns.description: First day with an ad_daily row (>= 2026-05-06); NULL for ads that never delivered in that window.

columns.name: last_day
columns.description: Last day with an ad_daily row.

columns.name: lifetime_spend
columns.description: All-time spend, dollars (Meta-reported). NULL when the ad has no lifetime row.

columns.name: lifetime_revenue
columns.description: All-time Meta-reported purchase conversion value, dollars.

examples.title: Active ads and their spend, by product
examples.sql:
SELECT product_slug, count(*) AS active_ads, round(sum(lifetime_spend)) AS lifetime_spend
FROM analytics.meta_ads
WHERE is_active
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC;

examples.title: Ads that delivered in the last 7 days but are not active now
examples.sql:
SELECT ad_id, ad_name, status, last_day
FROM analytics.meta_ads
WHERE last_day >= (SELECT max(last_day) FROM analytics.data_coverage WHERE source = 'meta_ad_daily') - 6 AND NOT is_active
ORDER BY last_day DESC LIMIT 50;

relations.name: analytics.meta_ad_daily
relations.purpose: The main Meta fact view: one row per Meta ad per day with Meta-reported results AND Upstack-attributed new customers / orders side by side, plus the ad's names, campaign, ad set, stage and product. Roll up from here; never add purchases to Google's.
relations.source: public.ad_daily (Meta Graph API, ad x day) combined per ad and day with public.ad_daily_upstack (Upstack any-click 30-day attribution mapped to ads), names from analytics.meta_ads
relations.refresh: nightly (etl service 13:00 UTC): Meta trailing 28 days re-pulled and replaced (Meta restates conversions for weeks), Upstack trailing 7 days re-pulled
relations.coverage: 2026-05-06 through yesterday (Pacific). Meta days are each ad account's own calendar day; Upstack days are Pacific.
caveats: Three bases live in this view. spend, impressions, link_clicks, meta_purchases, meta_revenue are Meta's. upstack_new_customers / upstack_new_customer_revenue are Upstack's first-order basis (the 'NC' numbers: NC ROAS = upstack_new_customer_revenue / spend). upstack_orders / upstack_order_revenue are every order Upstack credits to the ad. Spend is Meta's in all three.
upstack_* is NULL (not 0) on days Upstack has not been pulled; coverage starts 2026-05-06 as well.

Upstack credits an order to every ad clicked in the 30 days before it (any-click), so Upstack-only ad-days exist where the ad spent nothing that day (spend = 0, meta_* = 0, upstack_* > 0). Filter spend > 0 only if you want delivery days.

When one ad is copied into several ad sets under the same name, Upstack (which sees names, not ids) credit is split across the copies by their Meta spend that day. Family-level and higher sums are exact; one copy's own upstack_* numbers are an allocation.
About 1.3% of Upstack-credited orders and 1.3% of new customers match no Meta ad ('(not set)', deleted ads); they are in orders_daily but in no row here.
Meta purchases count returning customers; Upstack new customers do not. They are different quantities, not the same number measured twice.
link_clicks is Meta's 'link_click' action count (link clicks, not all clicks). Impressions are Meta's.
source: 'meta_api' for Graph-pulled rows, 'sheet' for the old family-grain backfill (none left in production), NULL on Upstack-only ad-days.

columns.name: day
columns.description: Calendar day. Meta numbers: the ad account's own day (Main = America/Los_Angeles, BackUp = America/New_York, not re-based). Upstack numbers: Pacific.

columns.name: product_slug
columns.description: Product the ad counts under (see analytics.meta_ads); NULL = no active product.

columns.name: campaign_id
columns.description: Meta campaign id (NULL on family-grain legacy rows).

columns.name: stage
columns.description: 'testing' | 'scaling' from the campaign name ('test' in the name = testing).

columns.name: adset_id
columns.description: Meta ad set id (NULL on family-grain legacy rows).

columns.name: source
columns.description: Where the Meta side of the row came from: 'meta_api' | 'sheet'; NULL when the row exists only because Upstack credited the ad.

columns.name: spend
columns.description: Meta spend, dollars (0 on Upstack-only ad-days). Additive across ads, ad sets, campaigns and across platforms.

columns.name: meta_purchases
columns.description: Purchases Meta reports for the ad that day (omni_purchase, else purchase, else pixel purchase), Meta's default attribution; includes returning customers.

columns.name: meta_revenue
columns.description: Purchase conversion value Meta reports, dollars. meta_revenue / spend = Meta ROAS.

columns.name: upstack_new_customers
columns.description: First-time customers Upstack credits to the ad (any-click, 30-day window, utm_source 'Meta Ads'). NULL on days not pulled.

columns.name: upstack_new_customer_revenue
columns.description: Order total (tax included, before refunds) of those first orders, dollars. / spend = NC ROAS.

columns.name: upstack_orders
columns.description: All orders (new and returning customers) Upstack credits to the ad. NULL on days not pulled.

columns.name: upstack_order_revenue
columns.description: Order total of those orders, dollars (tax included, before refunds).

columns.name: landing_page_views
columns.description: Meta landing page views (omni_landing_page_view, else landing_page_view). NULL when the day has no Meta pull of it yet; 0 on Upstack-only ad-days.

columns.name: add_to_carts
columns.description: Meta adds to cart (omni_add_to_cart, else add_to_cart, else pixel add to cart), the 'Adds to cart' of Ads Manager; includes returning customers. NULL when not pulled yet; 0 on Upstack-only ad-days.

columns.name: initiated_checkouts
columns.description: Meta initiated checkouts (omni_initiated_checkout, else initiate_checkout, else pixel initiate checkout), the 'Checkouts initiated' of Ads Manager; includes returning customers. NULL when not pulled yet; 0 on Upstack-only ad-days.

columns.name: payment_info_adds
columns.description: Meta payment info added (omni_add_payment_info, else add_payment_info, else pixel add payment info), the checkout step between initiated checkout and purchase. NULL when not pulled yet; 0 on Upstack-only ad-days.

examples.title: Ad level: 30-day spend and Meta-reported ROAS
examples.sql:
SELECT ad_id, ad_name, product_slug,
       round(sum(spend), 2) AS spend,
       sum(meta_purchases) AS purchases,
       round(sum(meta_revenue) / NULLIF(sum(spend), 0), 2) AS roas
FROM analytics.meta_ad_daily
WHERE day > (SELECT max(last_day) FROM analytics.data_coverage WHERE source = 'meta_ad_daily') - 30
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
HAVING sum(spend) > 0
ORDER BY spend DESC LIMIT 25;

examples.title: Ad level: new-customer ROAS and cost per new customer on the Upstack basis (30 days)
examples.sql:
SELECT ad_id, ad_name,
       round(sum(spend), 2) AS spend,
       sum(upstack_new_customers) AS new_customers,
       round(sum(spend) / NULLIF(sum(upstack_new_customers), 0), 2) AS nc_cpa,
       round(sum(upstack_new_customer_revenue) / NULLIF(sum(spend), 0), 2) AS nc_roas
FROM analytics.meta_ad_daily
WHERE day > (SELECT max(last_day) FROM analytics.data_coverage WHERE source = 'meta_ad_daily') - 30
GROUP BY 1, 2
HAVING sum(spend) > 0
ORDER BY spend DESC LIMIT 25;

examples.title: Spend by product by day (last 14 days)
examples.sql:
SELECT day, coalesce(product_slug, '(no product)') AS product, round(sum(spend), 2) AS spend
FROM analytics.meta_ad_daily
WHERE day > (SELECT max(last_day) FROM analytics.data_coverage WHERE source = 'meta_ad_daily') - 14
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1 DESC, 3 DESC;

examples.title: Funnel by product, last 7 days: link click to add to cart, landing page view to add to cart, add to cart to purchase
examples.sql:
SELECT coalesce(product_slug, '(no product)') AS product, sum(link_clicks) AS link_clicks, sum(landing_page_views) AS landing_page_views, sum(add_to_carts) AS add_to_carts,
       sum(meta_purchases) AS purchases,
       round(sum(add_to_carts) / NULLIF(sum(link_clicks), 0), 4) AS link_click_to_atc,
       round(sum(add_to_carts) / NULLIF(sum(landing_page_views), 0), 4) AS lpv_to_atc,
       round(sum(meta_purchases) / NULLIF(sum(add_to_carts), 0), 4) AS atc_to_purchase
FROM analytics.meta_ad_daily
WHERE day > (SELECT max(last_day) FROM analytics.data_coverage WHERE source = 'meta_ad_daily') - 7 AND add_to_carts IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY sum(spend) DESC;

examples.title: Checkout funnel by product, last 7 days: add to cart to initiated checkout, initiated checkout to purchase
examples.sql:
SELECT coalesce(product_slug, '(no product)') AS product, sum(add_to_carts) AS add_to_carts, sum(initiated_checkouts) AS initiated_checkouts, sum(payment_info_adds) AS payment_info_adds,
       sum(meta_purchases) AS purchases,
       round(sum(initiated_checkouts) / NULLIF(sum(add_to_carts), 0), 4) AS atc_to_ic,
       round(sum(meta_purchases) / NULLIF(sum(initiated_checkouts), 0), 4) AS ic_to_purchase
FROM analytics.meta_ad_daily
WHERE day > (SELECT max(last_day) FROM analytics.data_coverage WHERE source = 'meta_ad_daily') - 7 AND initiated_checkouts IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY sum(spend) DESC;

relations.name: analytics.meta_adset_daily
relations.purpose: Ad set x day roll-up of meta_ad_daily (Meta-reported and Upstack bases side by side).
relations.source: analytics.meta_ad_daily grouped by day and ad set
caveats: Same bases and NULL rules as meta_ad_daily. adset_id is NULL only for legacy family-grain rows (none in production).
An ad set belongs to one campaign; names are the current ones. There is no product column because an ad set can hold ads of several products: group meta_ad_daily by product_slug instead.

columns.name: ads_with_spend
columns.description: Distinct ads in the ad set with spend > 0 that day.

columns.name: upstack_new_customers
columns.description: Upstack first-time customers credited to the ad set's ads (NULL on days not pulled).

examples.title: Daily spend and Meta ROAS of one campaign's ad sets
examples.sql:
SELECT day, adset_name, round(spend, 2) AS spend, meta_purchases,
       round(meta_revenue / NULLIF(spend, 0), 2) AS roas
FROM analytics.meta_adset_daily
WHERE campaign_id = (SELECT campaign_id FROM analytics.meta_campaign_daily ORDER BY day DESC, spend DESC LIMIT 1)
  AND day > (SELECT max(last_day) FROM analytics.data_coverage WHERE source = 'meta_ad_daily') - 7
ORDER BY day DESC, spend DESC;

examples.title: Ad sets ranked by 7-day new-customer CPA (at least $200 spent)
examples.sql:
SELECT adset_id, max(adset_name) AS adset_name, round(sum(spend), 2) AS spend, sum(upstack_new_customers) AS new_customers,
       round(sum(spend) / NULLIF(sum(upstack_new_customers), 0), 2) AS nc_cpa
FROM analytics.meta_adset_daily
WHERE day > (SELECT max(last_day) FROM analytics.data_coverage WHERE source = 'meta_ad_daily') - 7
GROUP BY 1 HAVING sum(spend) >= 200 ORDER BY nc_cpa NULLS LAST LIMIT 25;

relations.name: analytics.meta_campaign_daily
relations.purpose: Campaign x day roll-up of meta_ad_daily (Meta-reported and Upstack bases side by side).
relations.source: analytics.meta_ad_daily grouped by day and campaign
relations.coverage: 2026-05-06 through yesterday (use meta_campaign_daily_history for campaign-level days back to 2024-12-31)
caveats: Same bases and NULL rules as meta_ad_daily.
A campaign can run ads of several products (shared All_US / test campaigns): split by product with meta_ad_daily.

columns.name: adsets_with_spend
columns.description: Distinct ad sets with spend > 0 that day.

columns.name: ads_with_spend
columns.description: Distinct ads with spend > 0 that day.

columns.name: upstack_new_customers
columns.description: Upstack first-time customers credited to the campaign's ads (NULL on days not pulled).

examples.title: Campaigns, last 7 days: spend, Meta ROAS, NC ROAS
examples.sql:
SELECT campaign_id, max(campaign_name) AS campaign, max(stage) AS stage, round(sum(spend)) AS spend,
       round(sum(meta_revenue) / NULLIF(sum(spend), 0), 2) AS meta_roas,
       round(sum(upstack_new_customer_revenue) / NULLIF(sum(spend), 0), 2) AS nc_roas
FROM analytics.meta_campaign_daily
WHERE day > (SELECT max(last_day) FROM analytics.data_coverage WHERE source = 'meta_ad_daily') - 7
GROUP BY 1 HAVING sum(spend) > 0 ORDER BY sum(spend) DESC LIMIT 25;

examples.title: Daily spend, testing vs scaling
examples.sql:
SELECT day, stage, round(sum(spend), 2) AS spend
FROM analytics.meta_campaign_daily
WHERE day > (SELECT max(last_day) FROM analytics.data_coverage WHERE source = 'meta_ad_daily') - 30
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1 DESC, 2;

relations.name: analytics.meta_campaign_daily_history
relations.purpose: Meta campaign x day back to 2024-12-31: the only Meta data before 2026-05-06 (campaign grain, no ad sets or ads). From 2026-05-06 on it equals meta_campaign_daily's Meta-reported columns.
relations.grain: one row per (day, campaign_id) after the day rule (a day is read from 'app' when it has app rows, else from 'sheet')
relations.source: public.proj_feed_meta_day: 'app' = aggregated from ad_daily by the app, 'sheet' = the Lonvera Projections sheet tab 'Meta Campaign - History'
relations.refresh: nightly (etl service 13:00 UTC via etl.projection_daily); sheet rows never change after the backfill
caveats: Meta-reported only (no Upstack columns). product and stage are classified from the CAMPAIGN NAME here ('VitaBull', 'Beef Liver', 'Boneflex', 'Unclassified'; 'Testing' / 'Scaling'), not through the tracker, so they can differ from analytics.meta_ads.product_slug.
Use it for trends across the May 2026 boundary; the ad-grain views cannot go back that far.

columns.name: product
columns.description: Product guessed from the campaign name: VitaBull | Beef Liver | Boneflex | Unclassified.

columns.name: stage
columns.description: 'Testing' when the campaign name contains 'test', else 'Scaling' (capitalised here).

columns.name: source
columns.description: 'app' (aggregated from ad_daily) or 'sheet' (the sheet's campaign history).

examples.title: Monthly Meta spend by product since 2025
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', day)::date AS month, product, round(sum(spend)) AS spend
FROM analytics.meta_campaign_daily_history
WHERE day >= '2025-01-01'
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 3 DESC;

examples.title: Meta ROAS by month (Meta-reported)
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', day)::date AS month, round(sum(spend)) AS spend, round(sum(meta_revenue) / NULLIF(sum(spend), 0), 2) AS roas
FROM analytics.meta_campaign_daily_history GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;

relations.name: analytics.meta_reach
relations.purpose: Account-level reach and frequency for Meta (both ad accounts summed). Reach is de-duplicated by Meta per period, so it is stored at each grain and must never be summed across days or weeks.
relations.grain: one row per (grain, period_key): grain is 'day', 'week' (ISO) or 'month'
relations.source: public.proj_feed_meta_reach (sheet tab 'Meta Account - Reach' today; the feeds service writes a shadow copy in proj_feedx_meta_reach)
relations.refresh: nightly (etl service via etl.projection_daily); the trailing days are replaced
relations.coverage: day 2025-01-01.., week 2024-12-30.., month 2025-01-01..; the current day, week and month are partial
caveats: Account level only: there is NO reach / frequency per ad, ad set, campaign or product (the product table, proj_feed_product_reach, holds unique outbound clicks only).
The last day is today (partial). Compare complete periods only.
frequency = impressions / reach, computed here (NULL when reach is 0).

columns.name: period_end
columns.description: Last day of the period (the current period ends today and is partial).

columns.name: reach
columns.description: People reached over the period (Meta de-duplicated; not additive across periods).

columns.name: unique_link_clicks
columns.description: Unique link clicks over the period.

columns.name: unique_outbound_clicks
columns.description: Unique outbound clicks over the period (Meta de-duplicated).

examples.title: Weekly reach and frequency, last 12 complete weeks
examples.sql:
SELECT period_key, period_start, impressions, reach, frequency
FROM analytics.meta_reach
WHERE grain = 'week' AND period_end < current_date
ORDER BY period_start DESC LIMIT 12;

examples.title: Monthly unique outbound clicks per 1,000 reached
examples.sql:
SELECT period_key, reach, unique_outbound_clicks, round(1000.0 * unique_outbound_clicks / NULLIF(reach, 0), 1) AS uoc_per_1000_reached
FROM analytics.meta_reach WHERE grain = 'month' ORDER BY period_start DESC LIMIT 12;

relations.name: analytics.google_campaign_daily
relations.purpose: Google Ads campaign x day: Google's own spend, impressions, clicks and conversions plus Upstack's attributed new customers / orders. Google has no ad group, ad or keyword grain in this database.
relations.source: public.google_daily (Upstack channel feed joined to Upstack any-click 30-day attribution by campaign name) + upstack_google_campaigns
relations.refresh: nightly (etl service 13:00 UTC): trailing 7 days re-pulled; the job refuses a day with more than $200 spend and no attributed orders
relations.coverage: Google's own numbers 2024-03-25 through yesterday (Pacific); Upstack columns from 2025-05-13 (NULL before)
caveats: Two bases: google_* are Google's own conversions (restated by Google for days afterwards); upstack_* are Upstack's attribution of orders to the campaign (utm campaign name), any-click 30-day, which credits Google with orders that also had a Meta click.
Purchases and revenue overlap with Meta's: never add google_* or upstack_* to Meta's. Spend, impressions and clicks are additive.
campaign_type is read from the campaign NAME (Shopping, Search, Performance Max, Demand Gen, Other); Upstack exposes none. 'Other' is never guessed.

in_feed = false rows are Upstack-attributed orders whose utm campaign matches no Google campaign ('(not set)', raw ids, deleted campaigns): spend 0, kept so totals tie to Upstack's Google total (about 3% of orders).
clicks are all clicks (Google has no link-click event).

columns.name: campaign_key
columns.description: Google campaign id, or 'name:<utm campaign>' when the utm value is no Google campaign (in_feed = false).

columns.name: campaign_type
columns.description: Shopping | Search | Performance Max | Demand Gen | Other, read from the name.

columns.name: campaign_status
columns.description: Campaign status from the Upstack feed (NULL for in_feed = false rows).

columns.name: bid_strategy
columns.description: Bid strategy from the Upstack feed (NULL for in_feed = false rows).

columns.name: in_feed
columns.description: true = a Google campaign in the channel feed; false = utm campaign with no Google campaign.

columns.name: google_purchases
columns.description: Purchases Google reports (delivered through Upstack's ad-platform feed).

columns.name: upstack_new_customers
columns.description: First-time customers Upstack credits to the campaign (any-click, 30 days, utm_source 'Google Ads'). NULL before 2025-05-13.

columns.name: upstack_new_customer_revenue
columns.description: Their first-order revenue, dollars (tax included, before refunds).

columns.name: upstack_orders
columns.description: All orders Upstack credits to the campaign.

examples.title: Spend and Google-reported ROAS by campaign type, last 30 days
examples.sql:
SELECT campaign_type, round(sum(spend)) AS spend, round(sum(google_revenue) / NULLIF(sum(spend), 0), 2) AS google_roas,
       round(sum(upstack_new_customer_revenue) / NULLIF(sum(spend), 0), 2) AS nc_roas
FROM analytics.google_campaign_daily
WHERE day > (SELECT max(last_day) FROM analytics.data_coverage WHERE source = 'google_campaign_daily') - 30
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC;

examples.title: Top Google campaigns by spend this month
examples.sql:
SELECT campaign_name, campaign_type, round(sum(spend)) AS spend, sum(clicks) AS clicks
FROM analytics.google_campaign_daily
WHERE day >= date_trunc('month', current_date - 1)
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 3 DESC LIMIT 15;

relations.name: analytics.platform_daily
relations.purpose: Meta and Google side by side per day. Spend, impressions and clicks are additive across the two platforms; purchases and revenue are not.
relations.grain: one row per (day, platform) with platform 'meta' or 'google'
relations.source: analytics.meta_ad_daily and analytics.google_campaign_daily grouped by day
relations.coverage: Meta 2026-05-06.., Google 2024-03-25.. through yesterday (Pacific); Total NC ROAS is defined only on days both platforms and orders_daily have
caveats: spend is additive: Total spend = sum over platforms. own_purchases / own_revenue / upstack_* are NOT: both platforms credit the same orders (the overlap cannot be measured), so adding them gives the wrong number. Never divide a sum of platform revenue by total spend.
Total NC ROAS = actual new-customer revenue (analytics.orders_daily.new_customer_revenue, counted once) / total spend of the same days. Use the example below.
clicks: Meta = link clicks, Google = all clicks. own_* is each platform's own reporting; upstack_* is Upstack's any-click 30-day attribution.
Meta days are each ad account's own day, Google and Upstack days are Pacific; the one-day offset matters only for the BackUp account (New York).

columns.name: day
columns.description: Calendar day (Meta: ad account day; Google / Upstack: Pacific).

columns.name: spend
columns.description: Platform spend, dollars. Additive across platforms.

columns.name: clicks
columns.description: Meta: link clicks. Google: all clicks.

columns.name: own_purchases
columns.description: Purchases the platform reports itself. Not additive across platforms.

columns.name: own_revenue
columns.description: Conversion value the platform reports itself, dollars. Not additive across platforms.

columns.name: upstack_new_customers
columns.description: Upstack first-time customers credited to the platform (NULL on days Upstack was not pulled). Not additive across platforms.

columns.name: upstack_new_customer_revenue
columns.description: Their first-order revenue, dollars. Not additive across platforms.

columns.name: upstack_orders
columns.description: All orders Upstack credits to the platform. Not additive across platforms.

columns.name: upstack_order_revenue
columns.description: Revenue of those orders, dollars. Not additive across platforms.

examples.title: Meta vs Google spend per day (last 14 days)
examples.sql:
SELECT day,
       round(sum(spend) FILTER (WHERE platform = 'meta'), 2) AS meta_spend,
       round(sum(spend) FILTER (WHERE platform = 'google'), 2) AS google_spend,
       round(sum(spend), 2) AS total_spend
FROM analytics.platform_daily
WHERE day > (SELECT max(last_day) FROM analytics.data_coverage WHERE source = 'meta_ad_daily') - 14
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1 DESC;

examples.title: Total spend and Total NC ROAS by day (actual new-customer revenue / spend, days both platforms and orders cover)
examples.sql:
WITH s AS (
  SELECT day, sum(spend) AS spend, count(*) AS platforms FROM analytics.platform_daily GROUP BY day
)
SELECT s.day, round(s.spend, 2) AS total_spend, o.new_customer_revenue,
       round(o.new_customer_revenue / NULLIF(s.spend, 0), 4) AS total_nc_roas
FROM s JOIN analytics.orders_daily o USING (day)
WHERE s.platforms = 2 AND s.day > (SELECT max(last_day) FROM analytics.data_coverage WHERE source = 'meta_ad_daily') - 30
ORDER BY s.day DESC;

examples.title: Total NC ROAS for a window (ratio of sums, never a mean of daily ratios)
examples.sql:
WITH s AS (SELECT day, sum(spend) AS spend, count(*) AS platforms FROM analytics.platform_daily GROUP BY day)
SELECT count(*) AS days, round(sum(s.spend)) AS total_spend, round(sum(o.new_customer_revenue)) AS nc_revenue,
       round(sum(o.new_customer_revenue) / NULLIF(sum(s.spend), 0), 4) AS total_nc_roas
FROM s JOIN analytics.orders_daily o USING (day)
WHERE s.platforms = 2 AND s.day > (SELECT max(last_day) FROM analytics.data_coverage WHERE source = 'meta_ad_daily') - 30;

relations.name: analytics.orders_daily
relations.purpose: The business's ACTUAL revenue and customers per Pacific day, counted once (Upstack order-level measures). new_customer_revenue is the numerator of Total NC ROAS.
relations.grain: one row per Pacific day with orders
relations.refresh: nightly (etl service 13:00 UTC): trailing 7 days replaced because Upstack restates recent days
caveats: Revenue is the order total as Upstack reports it (tax included), before refunds: all numbers are gross.

There is no product, platform or campaign dimension: you cannot split new-customer revenue by product here. Use the attributed columns of the Meta / Google views (an attribution, not the actual) or analytics.orders_by_product_daily (the sheet's NC Rev - By Product: actual first-order revenue by the order's largest product line).
A day with no orders is absent, not zero.
new_customers is the count of first-time customers (first orders).

columns.name: new_customer_revenue
columns.description: Revenue of first orders that day, dollars (tax included, before refunds). orders.new_customer_total_revenue.

columns.name: new_customers
columns.description: Number of new customers (first orders) that day. orders.new_customers.

columns.name: returning_customer_revenue
columns.description: Revenue of repeat orders, dollars (subscription rebills included). orders.returning_customer_total_revenue.

columns.name: orders
columns.description: All orders that day (new and returning). orders.count.

columns.name: loaded_at
columns.description: When the day was last (re)pulled from Upstack.

examples.title: New-customer revenue and new customers by week
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('week', day)::date AS week, round(sum(new_customer_revenue)) AS nc_revenue, sum(new_customers) AS new_customers,
       round(sum(new_customer_revenue) / NULLIF(sum(new_customers), 0), 2) AS nc_aov
FROM analytics.orders_daily
WHERE day >= current_date - 90
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1 DESC;

examples.title: New vs returning share of revenue, last 30 days
examples.sql:
SELECT round(sum(new_customer_revenue)) AS new_rev, round(sum(returning_customer_revenue)) AS returning_rev,
       round(100 * sum(new_customer_revenue) / NULLIF(sum(total_revenue), 0), 1) AS new_pct
FROM analytics.orders_daily
WHERE day > (SELECT max(day) FROM analytics.orders_daily) - 30;

relations.name: analytics.creative_tracker
relations.purpose: One row per live Creative Tracker row (a concept / ad variant) with its current tag in the product's own tag set, its hook and its since-launch Meta-reported metrics. The way to ask 'which cluster / ICP / pain point / hook performs'.
relations.grain: one row per tracker row (tracker_row_id); an 'ad family' (family_key) can span several rows
relations.source: public.tracker_rows + ad_tags (current) + taxonomy_lines + ad_hooks + ad_metrics + products
relations.refresh: tracker rows synced nightly from the Creative Key Google Sheet (etl service 13:00 UTC); linemap tags and hooks are loaded by hand per tagging cycle (versions dated 2026-11-03 to 2026-11-05)
relations.coverage: all live tracker rows (~3,980); soft-deleted rows are left out
caveats: Metrics (spend_launch ... ads_active_count) sit on the FIRST tracker row of each ad family only; the other rows of the family read 0 (is_first_row says which). So sum over rows is right and a per-row average is wrong. 'Unique ads' = count of distinct family_key.
Since-launch metrics are Meta-reported (Graph API all-time per ad, summed over the family's Meta ads), not Upstack. spend_7d / _30d end on the last complete day.

Tags: products.tag_set decides which set drives the hierarchy: 'linemap' (cluster / ICP / pain point / trigger of the Communication Overview line, read from the creative image or video by a tagger, with a confidence) for Vita Bull, Beef Liver and Boneflex; 'tracker' (the tracker's own columns) for the rest. The tracker_* columns are always the tracker's own tags. A row with no current tag has NULL tag columns.
A family whose tracker rows carry different tags appears under each of them; its spend counts only where its first row sits.
asset_url is a Google Drive link to the creative file; access to the file is governed by Drive, not by this database.

columns.name: row_key
columns.description: Stable row key: concept id + '#' + ordinal among rows sharing (concept id, ad family). Never a sheet row number.

columns.name: product_slug
columns.description: vita-bull | beef-liver | boneflex | vita-belle | vital-flow | unassigned, from the tracker's Product column.

columns.name: ad_family
columns.description: Tracker 'Ad Family' as typed; empty when blank.

columns.name: family_key
columns.description: lower(ad_family), or 'id:' + lower(concept_id) when blank. The unique-ad key; joins analytics.meta_ads.tracker_family_key.

columns.name: status
columns.description: Tracker status, e.g. '8 - Launched', '5 - Creative In Progress', '3 - Briefing'.

columns.name: vendor
columns.description: Who made it (tracker column), e.g. Madre, Victoria, Internal, 10xROAS.

columns.name: launch_date
columns.description: Launch date from the tracker (a date typed by the team; NULL when blank).

columns.name: meta_ad_name
columns.description: The ad name to look for in Meta (tracker 'Name' column).

columns.name: transcript
columns.description: Video transcript from the tracker (can differ from the audio actually running; the linemap taggers re-transcribed top spenders).

columns.name: asset_url
columns.description: Link to the creative asset (Google Drive).

columns.name: tag_set
columns.description: Which tag set the tag columns come from: 'linemap' | 'tracker' (products.tag_set); NULL when the row is untagged in that set.

columns.name: line_code
columns.description: Communication Overview line code (L01.. Vita Bull, B01.. Beef Liver, BF01.. Boneflex); NULL for tracker tags.

columns.name: emotional_trigger
columns.description: Emotional trigger of the line (linemap tags).

columns.name: tag_confidence
columns.description: high | medium | low (linemap tags): how sure the tagger was; agreement of a blind re-tag is stored in app_meta reliability:<product>.

columns.name: tag_method
columns.description: How it was tagged: 'image', 'video: 4 frames + Whisper transcript', 'text only', 'no picture (copy only)', 'video: thumbnail + no audio' ...

columns.name: hook
columns.description: The ad's hook: first spoken line plus on-image headline, one short line (NULL when none was readable).

columns.name: is_first_row
columns.description: true on the one row of the family that carries its metrics.

columns.name: spend_launch
columns.description: Since-launch Meta spend of the family, dollars (first row only).

columns.name: revenue_launch
columns.description: Since-launch Meta-reported purchase value, dollars (first row only).

columns.name: spend_7d

columns.name: spend_30d
columns.description: Spend over the 30 days ending the last complete day (first row only).

columns.name: purchases_30d
columns.description: Meta-reported purchases over the same 30 days (first row only).

columns.name: revenue_30d
columns.description: Meta-reported purchase value over the same 30 days (first row only).

columns.name: live
columns.description: true when the family spent on either of the last two days (first row only).

columns.name: ads_active_count
columns.description: Meta ads of the family that are ACTIVE now (same value on every row of the family).

examples.title: Vita Bull since-launch spend and Meta ROAS by cluster / ICP / pain point (first rows only, so each family counts once)
examples.sql:
SELECT cluster, icp, pain_point, count(*) AS ads, round(sum(spend_launch)) AS spend,
       round(sum(revenue_launch) / NULLIF(sum(spend_launch), 0), 2) AS roas
FROM analytics.creative_tracker
WHERE product_slug = 'vita-bull' AND is_first_row
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3 ORDER BY sum(spend_launch) DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 20;

examples.title: Top creative families of the last 30 days with their tags and hook
examples.sql:
SELECT family_key, product_slug, cluster, icp, pain_point, hook, round(spend_30d) AS spend_30d,
       round(revenue_30d / NULLIF(spend_30d, 0), 2) AS roas_30d
FROM analytics.creative_tracker
WHERE is_first_row AND spend_30d > 0
ORDER BY spend_30d DESC LIMIT 20;

relations.name: analytics.data_coverage
relations.purpose: Freshness and coverage per data source: first and last day held, days, rows, when last loaded. Read it before quoting 'yesterday' or a trailing window.
relations.source: min / max of each source table's day column
caveats: last_day is the last day LOADED. For Meta, Upstack, Google and orders that is yesterday Pacific; today is never loaded. The meta_reach day grain ends today and the last row is partial.
The last 3 to 7 days still move: Meta restates conversions for weeks (28 trailing days re-pulled nightly), Upstack and orders re-pull 7 days.

columns.name: source
columns.description: meta_ad_daily | upstack_meta_attribution | google_campaign_daily | upstack_google_attribution | orders_daily | meta_reach (day grain) | meta_campaign_daily_history | amazon_ads_campaign_daily | amazon_ads_asin_daily | amazon_search_queries_weekly | amazon_search_queries_monthly | amazon_orders_asin_daily | amazon_traffic_daily | amazon_market_baskets | amazon_repeat_purchases | amazon_settlement_fees_daily.

columns.name: loaded_at
columns.description: Latest load / pull time of the source.

columns.name: note
columns.description: Timezone and refresh note for the source.

examples.title: Everything and how fresh it is
examples.sql: SELECT source, first_day, last_day, days, loaded_at FROM analytics.data_coverage ORDER BY source;

relations.name: analytics.etl_runs
relations.purpose: Log of every pipeline job run (tracker sync, Meta pull, lifetime pull, status refresh, metrics build, Upstack pull, hook / tag loads). Check it when a number looks stale.
relations.source: public.etl_runs (written by etl.db.JobRun on its own autocommit connection)
relations.coverage: since the first production run (2026-11-04 UTC)
caveats: status is running | ok | failed. A run that crashed leaves 'running'. error is scrubbed of tokens and cut to 500 characters.
stats is job-specific JSON (counts, reconciliation, windows). data_through is set by jobs that load daily data.

columns.name: job
columns.description: Job name: run_daily, tracker_sync, meta_pull, lifetime_pull, status_refresh, build_metrics, upstack_daily, load_tags, load_hooks ...

columns.name: data_through
columns.description: Last data day the job covered (NULL for jobs without one).

columns.name: rows_written
columns.description: Rows the job wrote, when it counts them.

columns.name: error
columns.description: Error text when failed (scrubbed, first 500 characters).

examples.title: Last 15 runs
examples.sql: SELECT id, job, started_at, status, data_through, rows_written FROM analytics.etl_runs ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 15;

examples.title: Failed runs in the last 7 days
examples.sql: SELECT id, job, started_at, error FROM analytics.etl_runs WHERE status = 'failed' AND started_at > now() - interval '7 days' ORDER BY id DESC;

relations.name: public.ad_daily
relations.purpose: Meta Graph API results per ad per day: the base fact table behind every Meta number. Meta-reported (Meta's own attribution).
relations.source: Meta Graph API insights level=ad, time_increment=1, both ad accounts (Lonvera Main, Lonvera BackUp); written by etl.meta_pull
relations.refresh: nightly (etl service 13:00 UTC, etl.run_daily): the trailing 28 days are re-pulled and replaced in ONE transaction (all or nothing), because Meta restates conversions for weeks
relations.coverage: 2026-05-06 (app_meta.daily_start, never moves) through yesterday; about 135K rows, 18.7K distinct ads in production
caveats: day is the ad account's OWN calendar day (Main = America/Los_Angeles, BackUp = New York); not re-based.

purchases = Meta action omni_purchase, else purchase, else offsite_conversion.fb_pixel_purchase, under Meta's default attribution (no window is requested); it counts returning customers. conv_value is the matching action value. Neither is Upstack's new-customer number.
No row filter on spend: purchases booked on days without delivery are kept, so a row can have spend 0 and purchases > 0.
link_clicks is Meta's link_click action (fallback inline_link_clicks). impressions is NULL only on legacy sheet rows (none in production).

landing_page_views = action omni_landing_page_view (else landing_page_view); add_to_carts = omni_add_to_cart (else add_to_cart, else offsite_conversion.fb_pixel_add_to_cart), same Meta default attribution as purchases. Both are NULL (not 0) on days before they were first pulled; the 2026-11-12 backfill fills them without touching any other column.

initiated_checkouts = omni_initiated_checkout (else initiate_checkout, else offsite_conversion.fb_pixel_initiate_checkout); payment_info_adds = omni_add_payment_info (else add_payment_info, else the pixel event; Meta returns only add_payment_info today). Both NULL (not 0) before the checkout backfill filled them (fill-only, no other column touched).
meta_family_key / meta_family follow the ad's CURRENT name (build_metrics re-syncs them after a rename).
Rows with source 'sheet' / ad_id 'fam:<family>' were a family-grain backfill; none remain in production.
Reach, frequency, video metrics (thruplays, watch time), demographic / placement breakdowns, ad-level budgets and bids are NOT stored.

columns.name: ad_id
columns.description: Meta ad id (text). 'fam:<family key>' on legacy family-grain rows.

columns.name: day
columns.description: Calendar day in the ad account's own timezone.

columns.name: meta_family_key
columns.description: lower(ad family): ad name without ' - Copy N' / merge-tag suffixes. Joins meta_family_map.

columns.name: meta_family
columns.description: The ad family with its original case.

columns.name: campaign_id
columns.description: Meta campaign id ('' = unknown, legacy rows only).

columns.name: purchases
columns.description: Meta-reported purchases (omni_purchase > purchase > pixel purchase), Meta default attribution; includes returning customers.

columns.name: conv_value
columns.description: Meta-reported purchase conversion value, dollars (revenue for Meta ROAS).

columns.name: landing_page_views
columns.description: Meta landing page views (omni_landing_page_view, else landing_page_view). NULL = not pulled yet (days before the 2026-11-12 funnel backfill).

columns.name: add_to_carts
columns.description: Meta adds to cart (omni_add_to_cart, else add_to_cart, else pixel add to cart), the 'Adds to cart' of Ads Manager. NULL = not pulled yet.

columns.name: initiated_checkouts
columns.description: Meta initiated checkouts (omni_initiated_checkout, else initiate_checkout, else pixel initiate checkout). NULL = not pulled yet.

columns.name: payment_info_adds
columns.description: Meta payment info added (omni_add_payment_info, else add_payment_info, else pixel add payment info). NULL = not pulled yet.

examples.title: Meta spend and ROAS by day, last 14 days
examples.sql:
SELECT day, round(sum(spend), 2) AS spend, sum(purchases) AS purchases, round(sum(conv_value) / NULLIF(sum(spend), 0), 2) AS roas
FROM ad_daily
WHERE day > (SELECT max(day) FROM ad_daily) - 14
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1 DESC;

examples.title: Top ads of the last 7 days (join meta_ads for names)
examples.sql:
SELECT d.ad_id, a.ad_name, round(sum(d.spend), 2) AS spend, round(sum(d.conv_value) / NULLIF(sum(d.spend), 0), 2) AS roas
FROM ad_daily d JOIN meta_ads a USING (ad_id)
WHERE d.day > (SELECT max(day) FROM ad_daily) - 7
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 3 DESC LIMIT 20;

relations.name: public.meta_ads
relations.purpose: One row per Meta ad: name, family, campaign, ad set, status, creation time. The raw dimension behind analytics.meta_ads.
relations.source: Meta Graph API: names and ids from the daily and all-time insights pulls, status / name / created_time from etl.status_refresh
relations.refresh: nightly (etl.run_daily); status is refreshed for every ad that delivered in the last 60 days and every ad not ARCHIVED / DELETED
relations.coverage: 42K ads: every ad in the daily window plus every ad the all-time pull returned
caveats: first_day / last_day are the first / last ad_daily day of the ad (NULL for the ~23K ads that never delivered since 2026-05-06).
status is Meta's effective_status at status_checked_at.
family_name / meta_family_key are fam(ad_name): ' - Copy N' and ' | x-merge-DATE' suffixes stripped.

columns.name: first_day
columns.description: First ad_daily day for the ad.

columns.name: last_day
columns.description: Last ad_daily day for the ad.

columns.name: family_name
columns.description: Ad name with copy / merge suffixes stripped, original case.

columns.name: status_checked_at
columns.description: When status was last read from Graph.

examples.title: Ads per status
examples.sql: SELECT status, count(*) AS ads FROM meta_ads GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC;

examples.title: Ad sets of the most recently delivering campaign
examples.sql: SELECT adset_name, count(*) AS ads FROM meta_ads WHERE campaign_id = (SELECT campaign_id FROM meta_campaigns ORDER BY last_day DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC;

relations.name: public.meta_campaigns
relations.purpose: One row per Meta campaign with its stage (testing / scaling). Stage is a naming rule applied on every pull.
relations.source: Meta Graph API campaign names seen in the daily and all-time pulls; stage recomputed by etl.build_metrics
caveats: stage = 'testing' when lower(name) contains 'test', else 'scaling'. It is a convention of the campaign naming, not a Meta setting.
first_day / last_day = first / last ad_daily day with spend rows for the campaign.

examples.title: Campaigns by stage
examples.sql: SELECT stage, count(*) AS campaigns, min(first_day) AS first_day, max(last_day) AS last_day FROM meta_campaigns GROUP BY 1;

relations.name: public.meta_ad_lifetime
relations.purpose: All-time Meta totals per ad (Meta-reported), the source of every 'since launch' number.
relations.source: Meta Graph API insights level=ad over the whole account life (etl.lifetime_pull), both accounts
relations.refresh: nightly (etl.run_daily): the table is REPLACED as a whole, only when both accounts reconcile with account-level lifetime spend within 0.5%
relations.coverage: 41.7K ads, through the last complete day
caveats: Totals cover the ad's whole life, which reaches back before ad_daily's 2026-05-06 start.
tracker_family_key is only filled on legacy sheet-sourced rows; use meta_family_map for the tracker match. source is 'meta_api' for every production row.
Meta-reported (default attribution); purchases include returning customers.

columns.name: meta_family_key
columns.description: lower(ad family), re-synced to the ad's current name.

columns.name: tracker_family_key
columns.description: Legacy: the sheet tab's Ad Family column (NULL for API rows).

columns.name: landing_page_views
columns.description: All-time Meta landing page views (omni_landing_page_view, else landing_page_view). NULL until the next nightly lifetime pull.

columns.name: add_to_carts
columns.description: All-time Meta adds to cart (omni_add_to_cart, else add_to_cart, else pixel add to cart). NULL until the next nightly lifetime pull.

columns.name: initiated_checkouts
columns.description: All-time Meta initiated checkouts (omni_initiated_checkout, else initiate_checkout, else pixel initiate checkout). NULL until the next nightly lifetime pull.

columns.name: payment_info_adds
columns.description: All-time Meta payment info added (omni_add_payment_info, else add_payment_info, else pixel add payment info). NULL until the next nightly lifetime pull.

examples.title: Top 20 ads by all-time spend (Meta-reported)
examples.sql: SELECT l.ad_id, a.ad_name, round(l.spend) AS spend, round(l.conv_value / NULLIF(l.spend, 0), 2) AS roas FROM meta_ad_lifetime l JOIN meta_ads a USING (ad_id) ORDER BY l.spend DESC LIMIT 20;

relations.name: public.ad_lifetime
relations.purpose: LEGACY: the sheet-era lifetime snapshot per tracker family (through app_meta.lifetime_cutoff 2026-09-17). Superseded by meta_ad_lifetime; do not use for current numbers.
relations.source: Creative Key sheet tab 'Meta Ads - Lifetime' (frozen snapshot loaded once at backfill)
caveats: Kept for history only; since-launch figures now come from meta_ad_lifetime via meta_family_map.

columns.name: spend
columns.description: Lifetime spend through the cutoff, dollars.

relations.name: public.meta_family_map
relations.purpose: Maps every Meta ad family to a Creative Tracker family (the resolver's output). The bridge between Meta numbers and tracker tags.
relations.source: etl.resolve_families (ported resolver: exact / relaunch-encoded / ad-name / concept-prefix / product+type+version rules)
relations.refresh: nightly (etl.run_daily): new families are mapped and previously unmatched ones retried; existing matches are left alone
caveats: tracker_family_key NULL = no tracker match (about 12K families, mostly old ads, ad copies by other names, and non-tracker products).
rule: 'exact' | 'relaunch' | 'adname' | 'prefix' | 'triple' (and 'sheet-windows' for legacy rows); NULL when unmatched.

columns.name: meta_family_key
columns.description: lower(Meta ad family). Joins ad_daily.meta_family_key and meta_ads.meta_family_key.

columns.name: meta_family
columns.description: Display name of the Meta family.

columns.name: tracker_family_key
columns.description: Matched tracker family_key (lower), or NULL. Joins tracker_rows.family_key.

relations.name: public.upstack_attr_days
relations.purpose: Registry of the days whose Upstack Meta attribution was pulled completely (a day with zero Meta orders is still a pulled day).
relations.refresh: nightly (etl service 13:00 UTC): trailing 7 Pacific days re-pulled
caveats: Upstack's own Meta attribution reaches back to 2025-05-13; this app loaded it from 2026-05-06, where its Meta daily data starts.

columns.name: pulled_at
columns.description: When the day was last pulled.

columns.name: campaigns
columns.description: Campaigns with orders or new customers that day.

columns.name: ad_rows
columns.description: Ad-grain attribution rows pulled that day.

columns.name: api_calls
columns.description: Upstack API calls the day took.

columns.name: nc_campaigns
columns.description: New customers Upstack credits to Meta at campaign level (the total).

columns.name: nc_ads
columns.description: The same, summed over the ad rows (the gap vs nc_campaigns = orders credited to a campaign but to no identifiable ad).

columns.name: note
columns.description: Campaigns that came back without an ad split ('unidentified: ...').

examples.title: Pulled days and how many new customers Upstack credits to Meta at campaign vs ad level

relations.name: public.upstack_attr_daily
relations.purpose: Raw Upstack attribution at utm campaign x utm ad NAME grain (as clicked), before mapping to Meta ad ids.
relations.grain: one row per (day, campaign, ad) where campaign and ad are utm values
relations.source: Upstack /api/query-attribution (dimension utm_campaign, then utm_ad per campaign), Meta Ads source
caveats: Names, not ids: the same ad name in several ad sets is summed. '(ad not identified)' marks campaigns Upstack could not split by ad.
Any-click, 30-day window: an order is credited to every ad clicked in the 30 days before it.
Revenue is the order total with tax, before refunds.

examples.title: Top utm campaigns by new customers, last 7 pulled days

relations.name: public.upstack_campaign_daily
relations.purpose: Upstack attribution totals per utm campaign and day (used for reconciliation against the ad-level rows).
relations.source: Upstack /api/query-attribution, dimension utm_campaign, Meta Ads source
caveats: Campaign-level totals are higher than the ad-level rows by the orders Upstack credits to no identifiable ad (about 1.3% of orders).

columns.name: rev
columns.description: Revenue of all credited orders, dollars.

relations.purpose: Upstack's own campaign-level ad-platform feed for Meta (spend, platform-reported purchases). Used only as the spend check: it equals Meta's spend to the cent from 2026-08-01.

caveats: Not a source of truth for Meta spend: use ad_daily. Differences of 1-4% on a few October days come from the BackUp account's New York day.

columns.name: purchases
columns.description: Purchases the platform reports (delivered through Upstack).

columns.name: purchases_value
columns.description: Conversion value the platform reports, dollars.

examples.title: Upstack's own Meta spend per day (the spend check)
examples.sql: SELECT day, round(sum(spend), 2) AS spend FROM upstack_channel_daily GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1 DESC LIMIT 14;

relations.name: public.upstack_unmapped_daily
relations.purpose: Upstack attribution rows the build could not tie to a Meta ad. Kept out of every ad, family and tag total; the tie-out reports them.
relations.source: etl.upstack_build (rebuilt in full on every build)
caveats: reason: 'not_identified' (no ad name / '(not set)' / '(ad not identified)'), 'no_campaign' (the utm campaign matches no Meta campaign), 'no_ad' (campaign found, ad name not).

examples.title: Credit that matched no Meta ad, by reason
examples.sql: SELECT reason, count(*) AS rows, sum(nc) AS new_customers, sum(orders) AS orders FROM upstack_unmapped_daily GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC;

relations.name: public.ad_daily_upstack
relations.purpose: ad_daily-shaped table for the Upstack source: Meta's spend / clicks / impressions per ad and day plus the Upstack orders and new customers credited to each ad.
relations.grain: one row per (ad_id, day) for every pulled day, plus rows for ads Upstack credited on days they had no ad_daily row
relations.source: etl.upstack_build: Meta spend copied from ad_daily for every pulled day (so a Meta restatement flows through) + Upstack attribution mapped from names to ad ids
relations.refresh: nightly (etl.upstack_daily): rebuilt in full from the stored raw pulls and the freshly refreshed ad_daily
caveats: Upstack reports campaign and ad NAMES, not ids. Mapping rules in order: exact ad name inside the utm campaign, same family inside the campaign, exact name in any campaign, same family anywhere. Where several ads match (one ad copied into several ad sets) the day's credit is split by each ad's Meta spend that day (else lifetime spend, else equally) and always sums back exactly.
Any-click credits every ad clicked in the 30 days before an order, so ad-level credits overlap and rows exist with spend 0.
purchases / conv_value = ALL attributed orders; nc_purchases / nc_conv_value = first orders only (new customers).

relations.refresh: nightly (etl.stage_moves, after run_daily and upstack_daily): DELETE + INSERT in one transaction; app_meta stage_moves_built_at / stage_moves_data_through say when
relations.coverage: 2026-05-06 through yesterday; about 2.6K creatives, 610 moved on 2026-11-04
caveats: A move is inferred from daily spend, not from an event: Meta cannot move an ad between campaigns, the buyer duplicates the creative into a scaling campaign. Testing and scaling on the same first day, scaling first and scaling only are NOT moves (see path).

Bulk moves: on 2026-08-22, 2026-10-22 and 2026-10-23 76, 187 and 80 creatives moved in one day (mass relaunches into new scaling campaigns, not test winners). bulk_move_day marks days with 40 or more moves; the app lets you hide them.

first_day is the first day with spend in any stage: creatives already running on the first day of data (launched_before_data_start, 2026-05-06) have an earlier real launch day, so days_in_test is a lower bound.

test_* counts TESTING-stage rows on days before the first scaling day (all testing days when it never scaled); scale_* counts SCALING-stage rows since the move through the last day. Testing spend that continues after the move is test_after_spend only.
Spend and link clicks are Meta's in every view; purchases and revenue are Meta-reported here, Upstack's in the _upstack_ views. Not additive across platforms.

examples.title: Creatives that moved to scaling in the last 30 days, with testing and scaling ROAS
examples.sql:
SELECT display, product_slug, first_day, scaling_first_day, days_in_test, round(test_spend, 2) AS test_spend,
       round(test_revenue / NULLIF(test_spend, 0), 2) AS test_roas, round(scale_spend, 2) AS scale_spend,
       round(scale_revenue / NULLIF(scale_spend, 0), 2) AS scale_roas, bulk_move_day
FROM creative_stage_moves
WHERE moved AND scaling_first_day > data_through - 30
ORDER BY scale_spend DESC LIMIT 20;

examples.title: Moves per day and which days were bulk (mass relaunch) days
examples.sql:
SELECT scaling_first_day AS day, count(*) AS moves, bool_or(bulk_move_day) AS bulk
FROM creative_stage_moves
WHERE moved
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 10;

relations.name: public.competitor_brands
relations.purpose: The competitor brands whose Meta ads are watched weekly (Heart & Soil, Primal Viking, My Marrow ...): exact search phrases for the public Ad Library, the advertiser-name regex that keeps only the brand's own page, and the freshness of the last scrape. Editable: insert / update rows to add or retire a brand (etl.competitor_ads only seeds missing brands).
relations.source: seeded by etl.competitor_ads (BRANDS constant), edited by hand; last_* columns written by each run
caveats: last_error is set when the brand failed in the latest run (blocked, age-gated, layout change); its rows are then carried forward and flagged stale in competitor_concepts.
Brands whose ads are age-gated for logged-out visitors (Hims, Keeps, Men's Edge, Reclaim Co) cannot be read and are not seeded.

relations.name: public.competitor_ads
relations.purpose: Weekly snapshot of the ACTIVE US Meta ads of each watched competitor, one row per Library ID, read from the public Meta Ad Library with headless Chromium. No spend, impressions or performance exist for these ads: days_running and variant_count are the only strength signals.
relations.source: etl.competitor_ads: public Ad Library cards (exact-phrase search, impressions-sorted, advertiser filtered)
relations.refresh: weekly, Sundays Pacific; a failed brand has its previous week copied forward (carried_from set)
relations.coverage: from 2026-11-09; about 100-150 ads per large brand (a top slice, not a census)
caveats: The Library lazy-loads: each phrase returns at most about 150 cards, so large brands (Heart & Soil about 1,000 ads) are a top slice by impressions.
start_date resets when a brand re-uploads an ad, so days_running understates the age of re-uploaded creatives.
format is 'video' when the card has a video, else 'image' (carousels are not distinguishable from images). hook is the first sentence of the copy (video speech and on-image text are not read).
Cards with 'N ads use this creative and text' count N in variant_count.

relations.name: public.competitor_concept_class
relations.purpose: Lonvera taxonomy classification of each competitor concept (concept_key), made once by headless Claude from the copy text and cached, so only new concepts use plan usage: an existing line (product / cluster / ICP / pain point from the autotag catalogs), a NEW angle with suggested cluster / ICP / pain point, or out of category.

relations.refresh: weekly; concepts already classified are never re-asked
caveats: Text only: the model never sees the image or video, so low confidence is common for statics whose message is on the image.

relations.name: public.competitor_concepts
relations.purpose: What competitors run on Meta right now, grouped by concept (near-duplicate copy), with the Lonvera line each maps to. The contract read by the weekly Creative priorities one-sheeter. Latest week: WHERE week_start = (SELECT max(week_start) FROM competitor_concepts).
caveats: No spend, impressions or ROAS: days_running (max across the concept's ads) and variant_count (ads sharing the creative) are proxies, and start dates reset on re-upload.
is_stale = the brand failed to load this week and the rows are the last good snapshot carried forward, or the data is older than 8 days.
Unclassified concepts show confidence 'low' and NULL mapped_product / line_code. For NEW angles cluster / icp / pain_point are the model's suggestion.

relations.name: public.competitor_posts
relations.purpose: Non-Meta chatter about watched competitors and the category: Reddit posts (public subreddit RSS) and news headlines (Google News RSS) that mention a competitor_brands brand or a category term (beef organ supplement, bone marrow supplement ...). Read by the /competitors page next to the Meta ad snapshots.
relations.source: etl.competitor_chatter: Google News RSS (one query per active brand plus category terms) and public subreddit RSS (/r/<sub>/new/.rss), filtered to brand / category mentions, spam dropped, last 14 days per run
relations.refresh: by hand / when scheduled: python -m etl.competitor_chatter [--days 14]; idempotent upsert, older rows are kept as history
relations.coverage: from 2026-11-12; only what the public feeds still show (Reddit RSS lists the newest 100 posts per subreddit)
caveats: Reddit search is blocked for logged-out clients, so Reddit rows come only from the newest posts of a short subreddit list that mention a brand or category term; a quiet week or a Reddit block (it blocks datacenter IPs and allows about 1 request a minute) shows few or no rows.
score and num_comments are 0 for every row: the RSS feeds carry neither. Do not read 0 as no engagement.
google_news summary holds the publisher name; the headline link is a Google News redirect. Brand is the brand searched or mentioned in the headline; NULL = category-level hit.

columns.name: brand

columns.name: subreddit

columns.name: score

columns.name: num_comments

columns.name: posted_at

columns.name: summary

columns.name: seen_on

relations.name: public.competitor_ad_media
relations.purpose: Creative thumbnails of the watched competitors' Meta ads (the image, or the poster frame of a video) so the /competitors page can show what the ads look like. Bytes are stored because the Ad Library image links are signed and expire within days.
relations.grain: one row per Meta Ad Library ID (joins to competitor_ads.library_id)
relations.source: etl.competitor_ads: downloaded from the public Ad Library at scrape time for a curated slice per brand (top 12 longest-running distinct concepts + up to 8 new this week, at most 400 per run), or by --media-backfill for ads already stored; re-encoded to JPEG, at most 480 px wide and 150 KB
relations.refresh: weekly with etl.competitor_ads (Sundays Pacific); python -m etl.competitor_ads --media-backfill fills ads already stored; rows older than 60 days that are not in the latest week are deleted

Carousels store the first image only; videos store the poster frame, never the video.

relations.name: public.creative_priorities_snapshots

relations.grain: one row per week (week_start = the Sunday, Pacific)

caveats: Scored on Meta-reported numbers; the Upstack new-customer ROAS only raises a flag. Prioritisation, not a causal claim.

rows is a JSON array; each element carries section ('iterate' | 'new'), product, rank, the line (cluster, icp, pain_point, story), concepts, score, confidence, flags, why, metrics and hooks. Scoring and thresholds: docs/CREATIVE_PRIORITIES.md.

Nothing here is written to the Google Sheet or Meta. The tag text is copied from the row at assign time, so history survives a taxonomy reload; line_id has no foreign key on purpose.

relations.name: public.daily_story_metrics
relations.purpose: The metric registry of the daily story: every daily metric the story can use, its basis, unit, formula and the analytics view and columns it comes from.
relations.source: etl/daily_story_registry.py (REGISTRY), upserted by every run of etl.daily_story
relations.refresh: nightly, with the daily story job
caveats: basis names what the number is made of (Upstack new customers, Meta-reported, Klaviyo-attributed ...); never mix bases in one ratio.

columns.description: Short key used inside daily_story_facts.facts (for example nc_roas, cpm, conv).

columns.name: metric_group
columns.description: headline | meta | google | orders | klaviyo | amazon | creative | site | placement.

columns.name: label
columns.description: Plain-language name with the acronym spelled out.

columns.name: unit
columns.description: usd | pct | x | count (pct is stored as a fraction, 0.12 = 12%).

columns.name: basis
columns.description: What the number is made of and which attribution it follows.

columns.name: formula
columns.description: How it is computed, ratios always from sums.

columns.name: source
columns.description: analytics view and columns the inputs come from.

relations.name: public.daily_story_facts
relations.purpose: The facts the daily story is written from: for each Pacific day, the JSON of every metric against its same-weekday baseline, the exact decomposition of new-customer return on ad spend, mix-versus-rate cuts, the live creative mix, top movers, the change ledger and the Meta, Google, email and text, Amazon and order-mix sections.
relations.refresh: nightly (etl service 13:00 UTC, non-fatal step after Klaviyo); a day can be recomputed with --day
relations.coverage: every day from 2026-05-06 (Meta ad-level start) through yesterday; early days have fewer than four baseline weeks (facts.metrics.<key>.n_baseline says how many)
caveats: Baseline = the same weekday in the previous four weeks: the metric table shows its median and its pooled value; the decomposition uses the pooled value so its terms add back exactly.
The headline is NC ROAS = orders_daily new-customer revenue / (Meta + Google spend). Ad-attributed ROAS inside the cuts is a cut for comparing ads, products and structures, never the headline.
The last 3 to 7 loaded days still move (Meta and Upstack restate): a day's facts are recomputed only when the job runs for it, so older rows can differ slightly from today's tables.
coverage = not_ready when a core source (Meta ads, Upstack orders, Google, Upstack Meta attribution) was not loaded for the day: the row then holds only facts.readiness.

columns.name: day
columns.description: Pacific day the facts describe (primary key).

columns.name: facts
columns.description: JSON: readiness, windows, metrics, decomposition, anomalies, cuts, movers, creative_live, changes, events, control, sections, cannot_see, basis_notes.

columns.name: coverage
columns.description: full | partial | not_ready: whether every core and optional source existed for the day.

columns.name: created_at
columns.description: When the facts were last computed.

relations.name: public.daily_story
relations.purpose: The daily story: one very concise explanation (170 words or fewer) of why a day's performance was what it was, built from daily_story_facts only, with confidence labels and the list of what the database cannot show.
relations.source: etl/daily_story_narrative.py: the model claude-sonnet-5-5 when available and every number in its text is found in the facts, else a deterministic template
relations.coverage: every day with facts; backfilled days carry the template text unless a model run was requested
caveats: source says llm or template; note explains a fallback (model off, answer rejected for a number not in the facts).
Wording is 'consistent with': no story proves a cause unless a clean like-for-like control exists.

columns.name: story
columns.description: The story text: TLDR, a few short lines, and a 'Cannot see' line.

columns.name: confidence
columns.description: JSON: a confidence label per claim (move, drivers, mix_vs_rate, changes, cause).

columns.name: cannot_see
columns.description: JSON list of what the database cannot show for that day.

columns.name: model
columns.description: Model that wrote the text; NULL for the template.

columns.name: note
columns.description: Why the template was used, when it was.

relations.name: public.daily_story_patterns
relations.purpose: The pattern memory: for each day, the change types that showed (new ad sets, capped share up, tROAS share up, a large email send, a cluster entering the live mix ...) with a magnitude bucket and what the next 1-3 days did against their same-weekday baselines.
relations.grain: one row per (day, change_type); change_type '_all_days' is the base-rate row every day has
relations.refresh: nightly; the previous 3 days are refreshed as their outcome windows lengthen
relations.coverage: from 2026-05-06; the newest days have out_days below 3
caveats: Correlation, not cause: several changes usually land together and consecutive days' outcome windows overlap.
out_* is the mean over days D+1..D+3 that exist of (value / same-weekday median baseline - 1); d1_* is D+1 alone; both NULL when the metric was not available.

columns.name: change_type
columns.description: Event type (new_adsets, budget_up, capped_share_up, troas_share_up, big_email_send, cluster_entered, google_spend_up, amazon_spend_up ... or _all_days).

columns.name: magnitude_bucket
columns.description: Size bucket of the largest event of that type that day.

columns.name: subject
columns.description: The campaign, cluster, hook or send the largest event named; empty when none.

columns.name: magnitude
columns.description: Numeric size of the largest event (share shift, count or ratio).

columns.name: out_days
columns.description: How many of D+1..D+3 had facts (0 to 3).

columns.name: out_nc_roas
columns.description: Mean change in NC ROAS vs the same-weekday median over D+1..D+3 (fraction).

columns.name: out_conv
columns.description: Same for conversion rate (new customers / link clicks).

columns.name: out_aov
columns.description: Same for new-customer average order value.

columns.name: d1_nc_roas
columns.description: NC ROAS change vs baseline on D+1 only.

columns.name: updated_at
columns.description: When the row was last written.

relations.name: public.daily_story_pattern_scoreboard
relations.purpose: The pattern scoreboard: how often each change type (and size bucket) has preceded a rise or a fall of more than 5% in NC ROAS, CPM, CTR, conversion rate or AOV over the next 1-3 days, next to the same rate over all days, with sample sizes. Only rows with n of 6 or more. Correlation, not cause.
relations.grain: one row per (change_type, magnitude_bucket, metric); magnitude_bucket '(any size)' pools the sizes
relations.refresh: always current: a view that recomputes on every read; the table behind it is rewritten nightly
caveats: rise_lift = rise_rate minus base_rise_rate: a pattern is only informative when its lift is clearly away from 0 with a decent n.
Overlapping outcome windows and simultaneous changes mean n overstates the independent evidence.
The 5% threshold is far inside the daily noise of NC ROAS, so the base rates are not small: read the lift, not the rate.

columns.name: n
columns.description: Days with this change type and an outcome.

columns.name: rises
columns.description: Days whose next 1-3 days averaged more than 5% above baseline.

columns.name: falls
columns.description: Days whose next 1-3 days averaged more than 5% below baseline.

columns.name: base_rise_rate
columns.description: Share of all days whose next 1-3 days averaged more than 5% above baseline.

relations.name: public.unmatched_meta
relations.purpose: Meta families that map to no live tracker family, with the product guessed for them and their windowed and since-launch numbers. Closes the gap between ad_metrics and the account total.

Windows end on the last complete day. spend_all / purchases_all / revenue_all are over the days held in ad_daily (2026-05-06 on).

examples.title: Spend of Meta families that sit on no tracker row, by guessed product

relations.name: public.alert_state

last_alerted is NULL when the problem was seen but no message could be sent (for example SLACK_ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL is not set yet): the alert goes out on the first run after the webhook works.

columns.name: check_id

columns.name: first_seen

columns.name: last_seen

columns.name: last_alerted

columns.name: resolved_at

columns.name: alert_count
