relations.name: public.meta_breakdown_daily
relations.purpose: Meta Ads results split by one breakdown set (age, gender, country, region, dma, placement, device, hour of day, creative asset ...), pulled at AD grain from the Insights API for both ad accounts. Partitioned by month on day.
relations.grain: one row per day x ad account x level (ad; campaign or account only for a set Meta refused at ad level) x entity x breakdown set x dimension values
relations.source: Meta Marketing API Insights (read only), etl.meta_breakdowns
relations.refresh: every 2 hours by the dedicated `breakdowns` service: the backfill (newest 30-day window first) until finished, then the trailing 7 days once a day
relations.coverage: see meta_breakdown_coverage for the first and last day and the level per set
caveats: purchases and purchase_value are Meta-reported (they count returning customers, not Upstack new customers).
Reach and unique outbound clicks are per row (one ad, one day, one dimension value): never sum them across days, ads or sets.
Action breakdown sets (action_device, action_destination ...) split only purchases and purchase_value; their spend, impressions and click columns are NULL.
Rows of different breakdown sets are different cuts of the same spend: never add across sets.
Meta can return a row for a day with purchases but no spend (view-through), so keep rows with zero spend.
Up to three dimension values per row sit in dim1, dim2, dim3 in the order of the names in breakdown_set (age,gender: dim1 = age, dim2 = gender); asset breakdowns store the JSON text Meta returned.

columns.name: day
columns.description: Calendar day as returned by Meta (each ad account buckets days in its own time zone: Lonvera Main Pacific, Lonvera BackUp Eastern).

columns.name: account_id
columns.description: Meta ad account id with the act_ prefix.

columns.name: level
columns.description: Grain of the entity: ad (the default for every set), campaign or account (only for a set Meta refused at the finer level).

columns.name: entity_id
columns.description: Ad id, campaign id or ad account id, depending on level.

columns.name: campaign_id
columns.description: Campaign of the entity (NULL at account level).

columns.name: adset_id
columns.description: Ad set of the entity (ad level only).

columns.name: breakdown_set
columns.description: Comma-separated breakdown names that were requested together, for example age,gender or publisher_platform,platform_position,impression_device.

columns.name: dim1
columns.description: Value of the first name in breakdown_set (text).

columns.name: dim2
columns.description: Value of the second name in breakdown_set, NULL when the set has one name.

columns.name: dim3
columns.description: Value of the third name in breakdown_set, NULL when the set has fewer than three.

columns.name: dims_key
columns.description: Stable text form of the dimension values (names sorted, name=value joined with a vertical bar, percent-escaped); any length. Not indexed: the primary key uses dims_hash.

columns.name: spend
columns.description: Meta spend in account currency (US dollars). NULL for action breakdown sets.

columns.name: impressions
columns.description: Meta impressions. NULL for action breakdown sets.

columns.name: reach
columns.description: Accounts reached on that day within the row. Not additive across days, ads or sets. NULL for action breakdown sets or when Meta would not return it with the breakdown.

columns.name: clicks
columns.description: All clicks (Meta clicks field), not only link clicks. NULL for action breakdown sets.

columns.name: inline_link_clicks
columns.description: Link clicks (Meta inline_link_clicks). NULL for action breakdown sets.

columns.name: outbound_clicks
columns.description: Outbound clicks (clicks that left Meta; Meta outbound_clicks, action type outbound_click). NULL for action breakdown sets.

columns.name: unique_outbound_clicks
columns.description: Unique outbound clicks within the row (Meta unique_outbound_clicks). Not additive across days or ads. NULL for action breakdown sets.

columns.name: purchases
columns.description: Meta-reported purchases (omni_purchase, else purchase, else pixel purchase), same rule as ad_daily.

columns.name: purchase_value
columns.description: Meta-reported purchase value (same action type rule), gross dollars.

columns.name: pulled_at
columns.description: When this row was last written by the pull.

columns.name: dims_hash
columns.description: md5 of dims_key (generated column), the fixed-size stand-in for dims_key in the primary key so very long values (ad copy assets) can be indexed.

relations.name: public.meta_breakdown_coverage
relations.purpose: What the breakdown pull holds per breakdown set and level: whether Meta accepted the request, the first and last day held, the row count and the last error.
relations.grain: one row per breakdown set x level
relations.refresh: nightly and after every backfill window
caveats: A set Meta refuses at ad level gets a status unsupported row at level ad (with the reason in last_error) and is pulled at campaign, then account level; each level has its own row.
status unsupported is asked again every 14 days. status error means a transient or unexpected failure, so the set may have gaps.
first_day, last_day and rows are read from meta_breakdown_daily after each window, so during a backfill first_day moves back window by window.

columns.name: breakdown_set
columns.description: Breakdown set name, as in meta_breakdown_daily.breakdown_set.

columns.name: level
columns.description: Level the set was requested at: ad, campaign or account.

columns.name: status
columns.description: ok = Meta accepted it and rows are held; unsupported = Meta refused the request at this level; error = failed for another reason (see last_error).

columns.name: first_day
columns.description: Earliest day held in meta_breakdown_daily for this set and level.

columns.name: last_day
columns.description: Latest day held in meta_breakdown_daily for this set and level.

columns.name: last_error
columns.description: Scrubbed text of the last refusal or failure; NULL when the last check was clean.

columns.name: rows
columns.description: Rows held in meta_breakdown_daily for this set and level.

columns.name: checked_at
columns.description: When the set was last requested.

relations.name: public.meta_breakdown_progress
relations.purpose: Resume bookkeeping of the breakdown backfill: one row per finished window of one breakdown set at one level for one ad account, so running the same backfill again skips what is done.
relations.grain: one row per breakdown set x level x ad account x window
relations.source: etl.meta_breakdowns (backfill and --auto mode; the plain trailing-days pull does not write it)
relations.refresh: written as each window x set finishes
relations.coverage: backfill windows and the three bookkeeping rows
caveats: A window is skipped on a rerun when a recorded window covers it. The backfill anchor is stored here on the first --auto run, so a resume after midnight needs no arguments.

Three bookkeeping rows have breakdown_set __anchor__ (window_start = oldest day, window_end = the backfill's --until day, rows = max days), __backfill_done__ (the backfill finished) and __caught_up__ (window_end = the last day the daily catch-up covered); level and account_id are '-'.
Safe to delete (or run with --restart): the next backfill simply starts over and pulls again (upserts).

columns.name: level
columns.description: Level the window was pulled at.

columns.name: window_start
columns.description: First day of the finished window (the oldest day for the __anchor__ row).

columns.name: window_end
columns.description: Last day of the finished window.

columns.name: rows
columns.description: Rows written for the window (both accounts are separate rows).

relations.name: analytics.meta_breakdown_daily
relations.purpose: Meta results split by ten everyday breakdowns (audience segment, age, gender, age x gender, country, region, publisher platform, platform position, device platform, hour of day), one row per day x ad x breakdown x value. Meta-reported numbers.
relations.grain: one row per (day, account, ad_id, breakdown, value); NO aggregation above ad
relations.source: public.meta_breakdown_daily (etl.meta_breakdowns, Meta Insights API) joined to the ten breakdown names
relations.refresh: nightly, trailing 7 days re-pulled; older windows come from the backfill (newest first)
relations.coverage: first and last day per breakdown: min(day) / max(day) over this view (a backfill moves first_day back window by window, up to 365 days; a breakdown Meta only serves for a shorter period stops earlier); ad_id and adset_id are NULL only where Meta refused a breakdown at ad level
caveats: Every one of the ten breakdowns is requested at AD level; ad_id and adset_id are NULL only for a breakdown Meta refused at ad level (then campaign_id is set and ad_id and adset_id are NULL; at account level campaign_id is NULL too). Query this view with ad_id IS NOT NULL (or read public.meta_breakdown_coverage: status and level per breakdown) to see which breakdowns have ad-level rows.
purchases and purchase_value are Meta-reported (count returning customers); they are not Upstack new customers and must not be mixed with them in one ratio.

reach and unique_outbound_clicks are per row (one ad, one day, one value): never sum them across days, ads or values. spend, impressions, link_clicks, purchases and purchase_value are additive within one breakdown.
Different breakdowns are different cuts of the same spend: sum within one breakdown only, never across breakdowns.
value for age_gender is 'age|gender' (for example '25-34|female'); hourly values are Meta's advertiser-time-zone hour buckets ('00:00:00 - 00:59:59').
Meta can return purchases for a day with no spend (view-through): keep those rows.

columns.name: day
columns.description: Calendar day as returned by Meta (Lonvera Main Pacific, Lonvera BackUp Eastern).

columns.name: campaign_id
columns.description: Meta campaign id (NULL only for a breakdown held at account level).

columns.name: adset_id
columns.description: Meta ad set id (NULL only for a breakdown Meta refused at ad level).

columns.name: ad_id
columns.description: Meta ad id (NULL only for a breakdown Meta refused at ad level: campaign or account rows).

columns.name: breakdown
columns.description: audience_segment (from user_segment_key) | age | gender | age_gender | country | region | publisher_platform | platform_position | device_platform | hourly (advertiser time zone). All ten are requested at ad level.

columns.name: value
columns.description: The text value of the breakdown ('25-34', 'female', 'US', 'facebook', '25-34|female' for age_gender, an hour bucket for hourly).

columns.name: reach
columns.description: Accounts reached on the day within the row (not additive; NULL when Meta would not return it with the breakdown).

columns.name: unique_outbound_clicks
columns.description: Unique outbound clicks within the row (not additive).

examples.title: Spend and Meta ROAS by age, last 7 complete days
examples.sql:
SELECT value AS age, round(sum(spend), 2) AS spend, sum(purchases) AS purchases, round(sum(purchase_value) / NULLIF(sum(spend), 0), 2) AS meta_roas
FROM analytics.meta_breakdown_daily WHERE breakdown = 'age' AND day >= current_date - 7 AND day < current_date GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;

examples.title: Which breakdowns have ad-level rows, and how far back each goes
examples.sql:
SELECT breakdown, ad_id IS NOT NULL AS ad_level, min(day) AS first_day, max(day) AS last_day, count(*) AS rows
FROM analytics.meta_breakdown_daily GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2;

relations.name: public.meta_change_log
relations.purpose: The Meta Marketing API activity log of both ad accounts: one row per change event (budget, bid, bid strategy, status, targeting, optimization goal, name, creation, creative, billing), who made it and when.
relations.grain: one row per activity-log event (event_key = sha1 of account, event_time, event_type, object_id, extra_data, actor_id: Meta gives no event id)
relations.source: Meta Marketing API GET /act_<id>/activities (read only), etl.meta_changes
relations.refresh: nightly in the etl run: the last 3 days re-read (overlap, deduped); history was backfilled week by week
relations.coverage: the backfill start is in docs (see analytics.data_coverage / min(event_day)); account BackUp has had no events in the loaded window unless rows say otherwise
caveats: object_type is Meta's old vocabulary: ADGROUP = an ad, CAMPAIGN = an ad SET, CAMPAIGN_GROUP = a campaign, ACCOUNT = the ad account; object_level carries the plain word (ad, adset, campaign, account).

Budgets and bids come as minor units and are stored in dollars (old_amount / new_amount: daily or lifetime budget for the budget events, the bid cap or target for bid strategy events, the charge for billing events). The ROAS floor comes x10000 and is stored as a ratio (0.90 = a 0.90x floor).

extra_data is often incomplete for bids and caps (a change of a bid on an ad set with no strategy change can be missing): meta_adset_state_daily and analytics.meta_change_ledger are the cross-check, from their first snapshot day on.

Meta writes system events too: first_delivery_event (actor Meta), update_ad_run_status to or from Pending Review / Pending Process, billing charges. Filter on actor_name or event_type for human changes.
Two byte-identical events in the same second collapse to one row. add_images / edit_images keep an empty raw (their extra_data is a signed image URL that expires).

columns.name: event_key
columns.description: Stable dedupe key (sha1 of account, event_time, event_type, object_id, extra_data, actor_id).

columns.name: event_day
columns.description: Pacific calendar day of event_time (America/Los_Angeles), the day grain every other Lonvera view uses.

columns.name: event_type
columns.description: Meta's event type, for example update_ad_set_budget, update_ad_set_bid_strategy, update_ad_set_run_status, update_ad_run_status, create_ad, create_ad_set, update_campaign_budget, update_ad_set_target_spec.

columns.name: translated_event_type
columns.description: Meta's human text for the event type ('Ad set budget updated').

columns.name: object_type
columns.description: Meta's raw object type: ADGROUP (ad), CAMPAIGN (ad set), CAMPAIGN_GROUP (campaign), ACCOUNT.

columns.name: object_level
columns.description: ad | adset | campaign | account (plain word for object_type).

columns.name: object_id
columns.description: Id of the changed object (ad, ad set, campaign or ad account id, by object_level).

columns.name: object_name
columns.description: Name of the object at the time of the event.

columns.name: campaign_id
columns.description: Campaign of the object: the object itself for campaign events, extra_data.campaign_id for ad set and ad events (NULL when Meta did not send it).

columns.name: actor_id
columns.description: Meta id of who made the change (0 = Meta itself).

columns.name: actor_name
columns.description: Name of who made the change ('Meta' for system events).

columns.name: application_name
columns.description: App the change came through when Meta says (NULL otherwise).

columns.name: old_value
columns.description: Text of the old value for scalar changes (status, strategy, name, goal, targeting description); NULL for amounts, which sit in old_amount.

columns.name: new_value
columns.description: Text of the new value (same rules as old_value).

columns.name: old_amount
columns.description: Old daily / lifetime budget or bid, dollars (budget and bid strategy events); NULL otherwise or when Meta did not send it.

columns.name: new_amount
columns.description: New daily / lifetime budget or bid, dollars; for create_ad_set / create_campaign_group the starting budget; for billing events the amount charged.

columns.name: old_roas_floor
columns.description: Old ROAS floor as a ratio (bid strategy events only).

columns.name: new_roas_floor
columns.description: New ROAS floor as a ratio (bid strategy events only).

columns.name: raw
columns.description: The event's extra_data as Meta returned it, parsed to JSON ({} when none; {"_unparsed": text} when it was not JSON): the source of truth when a parsed column is NULL. Every other field of the event is a column.

columns.name: loaded_at
columns.description: When the row was first written.

relations.name: public.meta_adset_state_daily
relations.purpose: A nightly snapshot of every live ad set's settings in both ad accounts (status, budget, bid, ROAS floor, optimization goal, attribution window): the record that lets a change in a bid or budget be seen even when the activity log's extra_data is incomplete.
relations.grain: one row per ad set per snapshot day (Pacific)
relations.source: Meta Marketing API GET /act_<id>/adsets (read only), etl.meta_changes
relations.refresh: nightly in the etl run (~05:00 Pacific); a same-day rerun replaces that day's rows
relations.coverage: starts on the day the first snapshot ran (see min(day)); nothing before it exists and it cannot be backfilled
caveats: Live ad sets (any status except archived) every day; archived ad sets only on the days within 3 days of their last update, so the archive step is visible without 4,000 dead rows a day.

Under campaign budget optimization (CBO) the ad set has no budget of its own: daily_budget and lifetime_budget are NULL and the budget lives on the campaign (see meta_change_log update_campaign_budget).
bid_strategy is NULL on ad sets that inherit the strategy from a CBO campaign.
A missing day (the run did not happen) shows as a longer gap in analytics.meta_change_ledger (prev_day), never as a fake change.

columns.name: adset_name
columns.description: Ad set name on the snapshot day.

columns.name: status
columns.description: Configured status: ACTIVE | PAUSED | ARCHIVED | DELETED.

columns.name: effective_status
columns.description: Effective delivery status (ACTIVE, PAUSED, CAMPAIGN_PAUSED, ARCHIVED, IN_PROCESS, WITH_ISSUES): ACTIVE only when the ad set and its campaign are both on.

columns.name: daily_budget
columns.description: Ad set daily budget, dollars (NULL under CBO).

columns.name: lifetime_budget
columns.description: Ad set lifetime budget, dollars (NULL when not set).

columns.name: bid_strategy
columns.description: LOWEST_COST_WITHOUT_CAP | COST_CAP | LOWEST_COST_WITH_BID_CAP | LOWEST_COST_WITH_MIN_ROAS ... (NULL when inherited from the campaign).

columns.name: bid_amount
columns.description: Bid cap or cost-cap target, dollars (NULL when none).

columns.name: roas_average_floor
columns.description: ROAS floor as a ratio (0.90 = 0.90x; Meta stores it x10000); NULL when none.

columns.name: attribution_spec
columns.description: Attribution windows as Meta returns them, for example [{"event_type": "CLICK_THROUGH", "window_days": 1}].

columns.name: created_time
columns.description: When the ad set was created.

columns.name: updated_time
columns.description: When Meta last recorded an edit of the ad set (any field).

relations.name: analytics.meta_change_log
relations.purpose: Meta's own activity log of both ad accounts: every budget, bid, strategy, status, targeting, creation and creative change with when it happened and whether Meta itself or a person / app made it. The first place to look when a day's spend, CPM or ROAS moved.
relations.source: public.meta_change_log (etl.meta_changes, Meta Marketing API activity log)
relations.coverage: from the backfill start to yesterday: min(event_day) / max(event_day) over this view
caveats: Most rows are noise for a performance story (first_delivery_event, run-status flips through Pending Review / Pending Process, billing charges, add_images / edit_images): filter is_system_event = false and object_level / event_type, for example update_ad_set_budget, update_ad_set_bid_strategy, update_campaign_budget, update_ad_set_run_status, update_ad_set_target_spec, create_ad_set.
object_level 'adset' is what Meta's raw object_type calls CAMPAIGN; 'campaign' is CAMPAIGN_GROUP. Join object_id to meta_adset_daily.adset_id / meta_campaign_daily.campaign_id.
old_amount / new_amount are dollars (budget and bid events); old_roas_floor / new_roas_floor are ratios. extra_data is often incomplete for bids: cross-check analytics.meta_change_ledger.
event_day is the Pacific day of the event; Meta's own account time zones differ (Main Pacific, BackUp Eastern), so an event near midnight can sit one day off from that account's insight days.
A change is an event, not a cause: this view says what was changed, not what it did to performance.

columns.name: translated_event_type
columns.description: Meta's readable name of the event type.

columns.name: object_type
columns.description: Meta's raw object type (ADGROUP = ad, CAMPAIGN = ad set, CAMPAIGN_GROUP = campaign).

columns.name: object_name
columns.description: Name of the object at the time.

columns.name: campaign_id
columns.description: Campaign of the object when known.

columns.name: is_system_event
columns.description: true when Meta itself made the event (first delivery, review status flips, billing), false when a person or an app did; the person's name is not exposed in analytics.

columns.name: application_name
columns.description: App the change came through, when Meta says.

columns.name: old_value
columns.description: Old value as text (status, strategy, name, targeting description); NULL for amounts.

columns.name: new_amount
columns.description: New budget or bid, dollars (starting budget on create events; the amount on billing events).

examples.title: Budget, bid, strategy and on / off changes by day, last 14 days
examples.sql:
SELECT event_day, event_type, object_level, count(*) AS events, count(DISTINCT object_id) AS objects
FROM analytics.meta_change_log
WHERE event_day >= current_date - 14 AND event_type IN ('update_ad_set_budget', 'update_ad_set_bid_strategy', 'update_campaign_budget', 'update_ad_set_run_status', 'update_campaign_run_status')
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3 ORDER BY 1 DESC, 4 DESC;

examples.title: Ad set budget changes with old and new dollars, yesterday
examples.sql:
SELECT event_time, object_name, old_amount, new_amount, is_system_event
FROM analytics.meta_change_log
WHERE event_type = 'update_ad_set_budget' AND event_day = current_date - 1
ORDER BY event_time;

relations.name: analytics.meta_adset_state_daily
relations.purpose: Daily snapshot of every live ad set's settings (status, budget, bid, ROAS floor, optimization goal, attribution): the state of the account on each morning, the base of analytics.meta_change_ledger.
relations.source: public.meta_adset_state_daily (etl.meta_changes, Meta Marketing API adsets, read only)
relations.coverage: starts on the first snapshot day (min(day) over this view); it is not backfillable
caveats: Taken in the early morning Pacific: a row for day D is the state at the start of D, so changes made on D-1 are already in it.
daily_budget is NULL under campaign budget optimization (the campaign owns the budget); bid_strategy is NULL when inherited.
Archived ad sets appear only for 3 days after their last update; an ad set missing from a day is archived, deleted or not pulled.

columns.name: effective_status
columns.description: ACTIVE only when ad set and campaign are on; else PAUSED, CAMPAIGN_PAUSED, ARCHIVED, IN_PROCESS, WITH_ISSUES.

columns.name: bid_amount
columns.description: Bid cap or cost-cap target, dollars.

columns.name: updated_time
columns.description: Meta's last-edit time of the ad set.

examples.title: Live ad sets today by strategy, with total daily budget
examples.sql:
SELECT coalesce(bid_strategy, '(campaign level)') AS strategy, count(*) AS adsets, sum(daily_budget) AS daily_budget
FROM analytics.meta_adset_state_daily
WHERE day = (SELECT max(day) FROM analytics.meta_adset_state_daily) AND effective_status = 'ACTIVE'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC;

examples.title: One ad set's settings day by day (replace the id)

relations.name: analytics.meta_change_ledger
relations.purpose: Ad set changes found by comparing each snapshot day with the previous one: new ad sets, paused / activated / archived, budget, bid, strategy, ROAS floor, optimization goal and attribution changes. Independent of the activity log, so it catches bid changes the log's extra_data omits.
relations.coverage: starts on the SECOND snapshot day (min(day) over this view); a change is only visible once two consecutive snapshots exist
caveats: A change happened between prev_day's snapshot and day's snapshot: the snapshot runs ~05:00 Pacific, so a change made on Pacific day D shows on day D+1 with prev_day D. A gap in prev_day means a missed snapshot, not a quiet period.

Only ad sets in the snapshot are compared. new_adset needs a creation time inside the gap, so old archived ad sets that are touched again do not show as new. Campaign budgets (CBO) are not in this view: use analytics.meta_change_log update_campaign_budget.
Several changes of the same ad set in one night collapse to the net difference; the sequence is in meta_change_log.
old_number / new_number are dollars for daily_budget, lifetime_budget and bid_amount, a ratio for roas_floor; NULL for text changes.

columns.name: day
columns.description: Snapshot day on which the change is seen.

columns.name: prev_day
columns.description: Previous snapshot day of this ad set (the change happened after it).

columns.name: change_type
columns.description: new_adset | paused (ACTIVE -> PAUSED) | activated (PAUSED -> ACTIVE) | archived | effective_status | daily_budget | lifetime_budget | bid_amount | bid_strategy | roas_floor | optimization_goal | attribution_spec.

columns.name: old_value
columns.description: Old value as text (NULL for new_adset).

columns.name: new_value
columns.description: New value as text (for new_adset: its effective status).

columns.name: old_number
columns.description: Old amount (dollars) or floor (ratio) for numeric changes.

examples.title: Bid and budget changes of the last 7 snapshot days
examples.sql:
SELECT day, change_type, count(*) AS adsets
FROM analytics.meta_change_ledger

relations.name: analytics.attribution_source_daily

relations.name: analytics.orders_daily_detail

examples.title: Gross vs net revenue by month

relations.name: analytics.pacing_amazon_month_to_date
relations.purpose: Completed Amazon month-to-date revenue, one snapshot per Pacific day and month: reported days plus the missing days projected at the trailing 7-day average of the reported days.
relations.refresh: after the Amazon feed load (feeds 21:00 UTC) and again in the etl service (13:00 UTC)
relations.coverage: from the first run; history kept so each day's projection can be compared with the final month
caveats: projected_mtd is an estimate, never an actual; the projected days themselves (json) are left out, rebuild them from daily_rate and days_projected.

columns.name: month
columns.description: First day of the month that was completed.

columns.name: data_through
columns.description: Last day that should have been complete at the run (yesterday by default).

columns.name: last_actual_day
columns.description: Last day of the month with reported Amazon revenue; null before the first reported day.

columns.name: days_actual
columns.description: Calendar days from the 1st through the last reported day.

columns.name: days_projected
columns.description: Days after the last reported day, through data_through, that were projected (0 when the feed is current or stale).

columns.name: daily_rate
columns.description: Dollars per projected day: mean of the last 7 reported days with revenue above zero (fewer when fewer exist).

columns.name: actual_mtd
columns.description: Reported Amazon revenue from the 1st through the last reported day, dollars.

columns.name: projected_mtd
columns.description: actual_mtd plus the projected days plus any partial-day top-up, dollars.

columns.name: status
columns.description: complete (nothing to project), projected, stale (feed more than 5 days behind: nothing projected), no_rate (no revenue in the feed), no_days (month has no complete day).

columns.name: method
columns.description: Rule and version that made the row, e.g. trailing-7-available/v1.

columns.name: flags
columns.description: Plain flags: feed_stale, short_window, window_has_gaps, gap_days_inside_month, newest_day_partial, no_data.

columns.name: partial_topup
columns.description: Dollars added because the newest reported day looked partial (below half the days before it); 0 otherwise.

columns.name: lag_days
columns.description: Days between data_through and the last reported day.

columns.name: rate_source
columns.description: trailing_7_available, or previous_month_last_7 when the month has no reported day yet.

columns.name: note
columns.description: The plain-language line the page shows.

examples.title: Latest Amazon month-to-date projection per month
examples.sql: SELECT DISTINCT ON (month) month, snapshot_day, actual_mtd, projected_mtd, status FROM analytics.pacing_amazon_month_to_date ORDER BY month DESC, snapshot_day DESC LIMIT 6;

relations.name: analytics.cohorts_curve_cumulative
relations.purpose: Cumulative dollars per cohort customer at each age (months after acquisition), with the monthly increment, the increment as a multiple of the first order and the cohort's recency rank at that age: the exact inputs of the Live retention curve.
relations.source: public.proj_cohort_cum joined to public.proj_cohorts and itself (age - 1)
caveats: Mirrors app/projection/cohorts/engine.py: a cell counts only when cum_per_customer is non-null and non-zero; the increment at age 1 is measured from first_order_per_customer.

Live curve at age a = sum(new_customers x increment_ratio) / sum(new_customers) over the rows with usable_rank <= N (N = the cohorts_n lever, 3 in code, 6 on the sheet); ages from tail_from_age (28) on = previous age x tail_decay (0.95). usable_rank 1 = the newest cohort that has a usable increment at that age.

columns.name: new_customers
columns.description: Customers in the cohort (the weight in the Live curve).

columns.name: first_order_per_customer
columns.description: The cohort's first-order dollars per customer.

columns.name: cum_per_customer
columns.description: Cumulative $ per customer, first order included.

columns.name: increment
columns.description: Dollars per customer earned in this month of age: cum_per_customer minus the previous age (age 1: minus the first order). NULL when this or the previous cell is not observed.

columns.name: increment_ratio
columns.description: increment / first_order_per_customer: repeat dollars per $1 of first-order dollars in this month of age (the curve's unit).

columns.name: usable_rank
columns.description: 1 = the newest cohort whose increment_ratio at this age is usable (non-null, non-zero, new_customers > 0), 2 = the next, ...; NULL when this cell is not usable.

examples.title: Live retention curve over the last 3 cohorts (ages 1-27)
examples.sql: SELECT age, round(sum(new_customers * increment_ratio) / NULLIF(sum(new_customers), 0), 4) AS live_curve FROM analytics.cohorts_curve_cumulative WHERE usable_rank <= 3 AND age < 28 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;

examples.title: Cumulative dollars per customer by age for the newest 6 cohorts
examples.sql: SELECT cohort_month, age, round(cum_per_customer, 2) AS cum_per_customer FROM analytics.cohorts_curve_cumulative WHERE cohort_month >= (SELECT max(cohort_month) FROM analytics.cohorts_monthly) - interval '5 months' ORDER BY cohort_month, age;

relations.name: analytics.creative_stage_moves
relations.purpose: Test to scale: one row per creative family with its testing and scaling spend and results, when it first spent in a Testing and in a Scaling campaign and whether it moved, in three bases.
relations.source: public.creative_stage_moves and its twins (etl.stage_moves, rebuilt nightly)
caveats: basis: 'meta' (Meta-reported purchases and revenue, counts returning customers) | 'upstack_new_customers' (Upstack first orders, any-click 30 days) | 'upstack_all_orders' (every order Upstack credits). Spend and impressions are Meta's in all three; filter basis = 'meta' unless you mean an Upstack basis, and never add rows of different bases.

A creative MOVED when it spent in a Testing campaign and its first spend in a Scaling campaign came on a later day (campaign name contains 'test' = Testing). Rate of reaching scaling = moved / began_in_testing over creatives launched in the window and not launched_before_data_start (app/promotions.py).
moves_that_day >= 40 (bulk_move_day) is a mass relaunch into new scaling campaigns, not a set of test winners: exclude it when judging test winners.
Held up? = (scale_revenue / scale_spend) / (test_revenue / test_spend): held >= 0.90, softer >= 0.70, fell below; too early until scale_spend >= $200 and scale_days >= 3.

Spend and impressions are Meta's in all three; filter basis = 'meta' unless you mean an Upstack basis, and never add rows of different bases.

columns.name: product_slug

examples.sql: SELECT * FROM analytics.creative_scaling_benchmarks LIMIT 20;

relations.name: analytics.creative_content

columns.name: transcript

columns.name: ad_id
columns.description: A Meta ad id of the family.

examples.title: Video families with a transcript

relations.name: analytics.tag_products

columns.name: meta_regex
columns.description: Regular expression used to guess the product from a Meta family name (NULL for 'unassigned').

columns.name: active
columns.description: false hides the product from the Products table.

examples.title: Products
examples.sql: SELECT slug, name, tag_set, active FROM analytics.tag_products ORDER BY sort_order;

examples.title: First rows
examples.sql: SELECT * FROM analytics.tag_products LIMIT 20;

relations.name: analytics.tag_taxonomy_lines

columns.name: story
columns.description: Short story the ad would tell (15 words or fewer).

columns.name: cluster_color
columns.description: Hex colour of the cluster in the sheet.

columns.name: added_after_tagging
columns.description: true = the line was added after the product's ads were tagged.

examples.title: Lines per product and cluster

examples.title: First rows

relations.name: analytics.tag_line_ingredients
relations.purpose: The ingredients that address each taxonomy line: one row per line and ingredient with what it attacks and what it supports.
relations.source: public.line_ingredients joined to taxonomy_lines and products

columns.name: ingredient
columns.description: Nutrient / active compound that addresses the pain point (e.g. Zinc, Heme Iron, Glucosamine).

columns.name: attacks
columns.description: 'What It Attacks': the mechanism it counters.

examples.title: Ingredients of one pain point

examples.title: First rows
examples.sql: SELECT * FROM analytics.tag_line_ingredients LIMIT 20;

relations.name: analytics.tracker_tags
relations.purpose: Every tag ever written to a tracker row (current and superseded), joined to the tracker row, product and taxonomy line. Filter is_current for what stands now.
relations.source: public.ad_tags joined to tracker_rows, products and taxonomy_lines (the extra json is left out)
relations.refresh: when tags load or the auto-tagger runs
caveats: A tracker row has at most one CURRENT tag per tag_set; analytics.creative_tracker already shows the current tag of the product's own tag set.
confidence / method say how sure the tagger was: low-confidence and copy-only tags are weaker evidence.

columns.name: concept_id
columns.description: Creative Tracker concept id of the tagged row.

columns.name: family_key
columns.description: Tracker ad family key (join to creative_tracker / creative_family_metrics).

columns.name: is_current
columns.description: true for the tag in force.

columns.name: line_code
columns.description: taxonomy_lines.line_code the tag points at (NULL for tracker-set tags).

columns.name: method
columns.description: How it was tagged: 'image', 'video: 4 frames + Whisper transcript', 'text only', 'no picture (copy only)', 'video: thumbnail + no audio' ...

columns.name: seen
columns.description: 'What Was Seen': the tagger's description of the creative.

columns.name: copy_only_line
columns.description: Line the copy-only first pass picked when different.

examples.title: Current line tags per product and confidence
examples.sql: SELECT product_slug, confidence, count(*) AS tags FROM analytics.tracker_tags WHERE is_current AND tag_set = 'linemap' GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2;

examples.title: First rows
examples.sql: SELECT * FROM analytics.tracker_tags LIMIT 20;

relations.name: analytics.tracker_hooks
relations.purpose: The hook of each tracker row: the first spoken line and the first on-screen text, joined to the tracker row and product.
relations.source: public.ad_hooks joined to tracker_rows and products
relations.coverage: the current tracker rows that had something readable (a silent video or an ad with no copy has no hook)
caveats: hook_source says where the hook came from (video transcript, image, copy). Rows with nothing readable have no hook.

examples.title: Hooks of the 10 biggest launched families (Meta basis)
examples.sql: SELECT h.product_slug, h.concept_id, h.hook, round(m.spend_launch) AS spend_launch FROM analytics.tracker_hooks h JOIN analytics.creative_family_metrics m ON m.tracker_row_id = h.tracker_row_id AND m.basis = 'meta' WHERE m.is_first_row ORDER BY m.spend_launch DESC LIMIT 10;

examples.title: First rows
examples.sql: SELECT * FROM analytics.tracker_hooks LIMIT 20;

relations.name: analytics.priorities_snapshots
relations.purpose: One row per weekly creative priorities snapshot: when it was built, the data it used and how many rows it holds.
relations.grain: one row per week_start (the Sunday, Pacific)
relations.source: public.creative_priorities_snapshots without the json blobs (they are flattened into the other priorities_* views)
relations.coverage: from the first week the page ran

columns.name: week_start
columns.description: The Sunday (Pacific) the snapshot belongs to (primary key).

columns.name: built_at
columns.description: When the snapshot was last written.

columns.name: data_through
columns.description: Last day of Meta data the snapshot used.

columns.name: row_count
columns.description: Number of rows in the snapshot (every line plus manual and proposal rows).

examples.title: Snapshots
examples.sql: SELECT week_start, data_through, row_count FROM analytics.priorities_snapshots ORDER BY week_start DESC;

examples.title: First rows
examples.sql: SELECT * FROM analytics.priorities_snapshots LIMIT 20;

relations.name: analytics.priorities_thresholds
relations.purpose: Every threshold and weight the week was scored with (HIT_SPEND, TOP_SPEND, JUDGED_SPEND, MIN_LINE_SPEND, the score weights ...), one row per (week, name).
caveats: value is text: cast it. Scoring counts a hit at HIT_SPEND = $1,000; the displayed hit rate uses TOP_SPEND = $10,000 (etl/creative_priorities.py).

columns.name: week_start
columns.description: The Sunday (Pacific) the snapshot belongs to (primary key).

columns.name: value
columns.description: Its value for that week, as text.

examples.title: The hit-rate constants of the latest week
examples.sql: SELECT name, value FROM analytics.priorities_thresholds WHERE week_start = (SELECT max(week_start) FROM analytics.priorities_snapshots) AND name IN ('HIT_SPEND', 'TOP_SPEND', 'JUDGED_SPEND', 'MATURE_DAYS');

examples.title: First rows
examples.sql: SELECT * FROM analytics.priorities_thresholds LIMIT 20;

relations.name: analytics.priorities_baselines
relations.purpose: The product averages each line is compared with (ROAS, CPA, hit rate, spend, funnel counts), one numeric row per (week, product, metric).
caveats: Metrics include roas, cpa, hit_rate (scoring basis, $1,000 over mature tested ads) and the funnel counts; see priorities_concepts for the per-line figures.

columns.name: metric
columns.description: Baseline metric name as in the snapshot.

examples.title: Product ROAS and CPA baselines of the latest week
examples.sql: SELECT product_slug, metric, value FROM analytics.priorities_baselines WHERE week_start = (SELECT max(week_start) FROM analytics.priorities_snapshots) AND metric IN ('roas', 'cpa', 'hit_rate') ORDER BY 1, 2;

examples.title: First rows
examples.sql: SELECT * FROM analytics.priorities_baselines LIMIT 20;

relations.name: analytics.priorities_concepts
relations.purpose: Every row of every weekly priorities snapshot, flattened: the line (cluster, ICP, pain point), its action section and status, score, confidence and the numbers behind it (Meta-reported, with Upstack new-customer ROAS beside them).
relations.grain: one row per (week_start, row of the snapshot)
relations.source: public.creative_priorities_snapshots.rows, flattened with the numeric fields typed
caveats: Two hit rates exist. hit_rate / hit_rate_index = SCORING: share of mature (>= 14 days old) tested ads that reached $1,000, shrunk toward the product average; the CSV export's hit_rate columns are this one. DISPLAY (what Josh calls a hit): ads_10k_plus_spend / ads_launched, ads that reached $10,000 since launch out of every launched ad. Name which one you mean.

Numbers are Meta-reported (roas = purchase value / spend); nc_roas is Upstack new-customer ROAS. ROAS is NULL under $100 spend. section / status use the current vocabulary (older snapshots are stored in the old words).

columns.name: product_slug
columns.description: vita-bull | beef-liver | boneflex (rows of manual concepts keep their typed product).

columns.name: section
columns.description: Action section the row sits in (make more, revive, test, stop, hold, add to sheet, proposed, competitor, everything else).

columns.name: status
columns.description: Line status (WORKING, RISING, FADED, COLLAPSED, TOO EARLY, UNTESTED, NOT WORKING, AVERAGE ...).

columns.name: rank
columns.description: Rank inside its product and section.

columns.name: line_code
columns.description: taxonomy_lines.line_code (NULL for manual and proposed rows).

columns.name: concepts
columns.description: New concepts to brief for the row this week.

columns.name: score
columns.description: 0-100 iterate score (35% economics, 20% hit rate, 20% room, 15% momentum, 10% size).

columns.name: flags
columns.description: Risk flags, joined with '; ' (thin sample, weak tags, few ads, Upstack new-customer ROAS below product average).

columns.name: why
columns.description: One-paragraph reason the row was chosen.

columns.name: is_manual
columns.description: true for a concept typed by hand on the page.

columns.name: spend
columns.description: Since-launch spend of the line, Meta, dollars.

columns.name: roas_index
columns.description: Shrunk since-launch ROAS / the product's ROAS.

columns.name: ads
columns.description: Ads of the line that spent.

columns.name: hits
columns.description: Mature judged ads that reached $1,000 (scoring hits).

columns.name: mature
columns.description: Judged ads at least 14 days old (the scoring hit-rate denominator).

columns.name: hit_rate
columns.description: SCORING hit rate: hits / mature (the $1,000 threshold).

columns.name: spend_30d
columns.description: Spend in the 30 days ending at data_through.

columns.name: spend_14d
columns.description: Spend in the 14 days ending at data_through.

columns.name: nc_purchases
columns.description: Upstack new customers credited since launch.

columns.name: live_ads
columns.description: Ads of the line that spent in the last days.

columns.name: ads_launched
columns.description: DISPLAY funnel: ads of the line launched (tracker rows with a launch date or any spend).

columns.name: ads_10k_plus_spend
columns.description: Launched ads at $10,000 or more (the display hits).

examples.title: Lines to iterate on this week, by product
examples.sql: SELECT product_slug, rank, cluster, icp, pain_point, status, score, round(spend) AS spend, roas FROM analytics.priorities_concepts WHERE week_start = (SELECT max(week_start) FROM analytics.priorities_snapshots) AND section IN ('iterate', 'make more') ORDER BY product_slug, rank LIMIT 30;

examples.title: Display hit rate per product (ads reaching $10K / launched ads) over the weeks
examples.sql: SELECT week_start, product_slug, sum(ads_10k_plus_spend) AS hits, sum(ads_launched) AS launched FROM analytics.priorities_concepts WHERE ads_launched IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1 DESC, 2 LIMIT 12;

relations.name: analytics.priorities_manual_concepts
relations.purpose: Concepts typed in by hand on the priorities page (not scored): product, section, line, why now and status.

columns.name: section
columns.description: Page section the concept sits in: 'iterate' | 'faded' | 'new' | 'other'.

columns.name: notes
columns.description: Free-text notes, up to 2,000 characters, line breaks kept.

columns.name: why_now
columns.description: Optional short why-now / what-to-test line, up to 300 characters.

columns.name: status
columns.description: 'open' (shown) or 'done' (hidden until Show done is ticked).

columns.name: new_cluster
columns.description: True when the cluster is not in the catalog for that product.

columns.name: new_icp
columns.description: True when the ICP is not in the catalog under that cluster.

columns.name: new_pain_point
columns.description: True when the pain point is not in the catalog under that ICP.

columns.name: new_story
columns.description: True when the story is typed text not in the catalog for that pain point.

columns.name: updated_at
columns.description: When it was last edited or its status changed.

columns.name: done_at
columns.description: When it was marked done; NULL while open.

examples.title: Open manual concepts
examples.sql: SELECT manual_id, product, section, cluster, icp, pain_point, status FROM analytics.priorities_manual_concepts WHERE done_at IS NULL ORDER BY created_at DESC;

examples.title: First rows
examples.sql: SELECT * FROM analytics.priorities_manual_concepts LIMIT 20;

relations.name: analytics.production_assignments
relations.purpose: One concept given to one vendor to make for one week: the line, the brief and creative links, the timestamp of each step and the tracker concepts it became.
relations.source: public.creative_priorities_assignments without created_by / updated_by (who made a change is not exposed)
relations.refresh: on demand (the production board and the nightly etl.assignment_tags)
relations.coverage: from the day production tracking started
caveats: stage_from_assignment reads only the assignment's own fields; the app also takes the furthest stage its linked tracker rows show (join tracker_concept_ids to creative_tracker.concept_id and read status).
vendor_note is the note the vendor sees; note is internal.

columns.name: concept_key
columns.description: Stable concept handle: 'line:<taxonomy_lines.id>' when the row has a line, 'manual:<id>' for a manual concept, else 'text:<product>|<cluster>|<icp>|<pain point>' (lowercased, spaces collapsed).

columns.name: vendor
columns.description: Vendor, spelled as in the Creative Tracker Vendor column (Madre, Victoria, TrybeDCShop, TrybeOrion, 10xROAS, Internal, PuredMedia, CreateMastery, OpenProgram).

columns.name: line_id
columns.description: taxonomy_lines.id at assign time; NULL for manual or proposed concepts. No foreign key.

columns.name: manual_id
columns.description: creative_priorities_manual.id for a manual concept; NULL otherwise.

columns.name: line_code
columns.description: Line code (for example BL12) at assign time; empty when none.

columns.name: story
columns.description: Story at assign time; empty when none.

columns.name: section_at_assign
columns.description: Action the concept had when assigned: 'revive' | 'make_more' | 'test' | 'add' | 'stop' | 'hold' (rows written before 2026-11-10 hold the old section names 'faded' | 'iterate' | 'new' | 'proposal' | 'competitor' | 'rest' | 'other', shown as the new Action).

columns.name: format_code
columns.description: Creative format chosen when assigning or later (creative_formats.code, foreign key); NULL when none was chosen. Set by a signed-in user only; a vendor sees it but cannot change it.

columns.name: note
columns.description: Note typed when assigning or changing the assignment.

columns.name: vendor_note
columns.description: Note typed by the vendor on their own link page.

columns.name: for_week
columns.description: The Monday of the week the vendor works on it (a CHECK enforces a Monday).

columns.name: brief_url
columns.description: Link to the brief; NULL until added.

columns.name: creative_url
columns.description: Link to the finished creative; NULL until added.

columns.name: brief_at
columns.description: When the brief link was first added; NULL until then.

columns.name: creative_at
columns.description: When the creative link was first added; NULL until then.

columns.name: ready_at
columns.description: When someone clicked Ready to launch; NULL if not (or cleared).

columns.name: launched_at
columns.description: When it was marked launched by hand; NULL if not. A linked tracker row with status 8 or 9 also counts as launched.

columns.name: dropped_at
columns.description: When the assignment was dropped (soft cancel); NULL while active. Rows are never deleted.

columns.name: tracker_concept_ids
columns.description: Creative Tracker Concept IDs of the ads made from this assignment, entered by hand.

columns.name: stage_from_assignment
columns.description: dropped | launched | ready | creative_in | brief_sent | assigned, from dropped_at, launched_at, ready_at, creative_url and brief_url in that order.

examples.title: Open assignments by vendor and week
examples.sql: SELECT vendor, for_week, stage_from_assignment, count(*) AS assignments FROM analytics.production_assignments WHERE stage_from_assignment NOT IN ('launched', 'dropped') GROUP BY 1, 2, 3 ORDER BY 2 DESC, 1;

examples.title: First rows
examples.sql: SELECT * FROM analytics.production_assignments LIMIT 20;

relations.name: analytics.production_formats
relations.purpose: The creative formats (static, short video, ...) an assignment can carry.

columns.name: format_code
columns.description: Short code (primary key), F1 to F6.

columns.name: name
columns.description: What the format is, shown in the pick list.

columns.name: length
columns.description: Typical running time, as text (for example '45 to 90s'); NULL when not set.

columns.name: active
columns.description: True while the format can be chosen on a new assignment.

examples.title: Formats
examples.sql: SELECT format_code, name, length FROM analytics.production_formats WHERE active ORDER BY sort;

examples.title: First rows
examples.sql: SELECT * FROM analytics.production_formats LIMIT 20;

relations.name: analytics.daily_story
relations.purpose: The daily story: the short explanation of why each day's performance was what it was, with confidence labels and what the database cannot see.

columns.name: story
columns.description: The story text: TLDR, a few short lines, and a 'Cannot see' line.

columns.name: confidence
columns.description: JSON: a confidence label per claim (move, drivers, mix_vs_rate, changes, cause).

columns.name: cannot_see
columns.description: JSON list of what the database cannot show for that day.

columns.name: model
columns.description: Model that wrote the text; NULL for the template.

columns.name: note
columns.description: Why the template was used, when it was.

examples.title: Latest story
examples.sql: SELECT day, headline, story FROM analytics.daily_story ORDER BY day DESC LIMIT 1;

examples.title: First rows
examples.sql: SELECT * FROM analytics.daily_story LIMIT 20;

relations.name: analytics.daily_story_facts
relations.purpose: The JSON facts each daily story is written from (metrics vs same-weekday baseline, decomposition, cuts, ledger, sections).

columns.name: day
columns.description: Pacific day the facts describe (primary key).

columns.name: facts

examples.sql: SELECT * FROM analytics.daily_story_facts LIMIT 20;

examples.title: Days with a large email send

examples.sql: SELECT * FROM analytics.daily_story_patterns LIMIT 20;

relations.name: analytics.daily_story_pattern_scoreboard
relations.purpose: Which change types have preceded rises or falls, with sample sizes and the base rate (correlation, not cause).

examples.title: First rows
examples.sql: SELECT * FROM analytics.daily_story_pattern_scoreboard LIMIT 20;

relations.name: analytics.daily_story_metric_registry

columns.name: metric_key

columns.name: label

relations.name: analytics.competitor_brands

relations.name: public.amazon_sqp_weekly
relations.purpose: Amazon Brand Analytics Search Query Performance by week: for each search query and each of our ASINs, the query's market size and our share of impressions, clicks, cart adds and purchases (the organic search signal).
relations.grain: one row per (period_start = Sunday, marketplace_id, asin, query_key)
relations.source: etl.feeds amazon_sqp_weekly (ExpandFi warehouse, merchant 1452: brand_analytics_search_query_performances, period WEEK)
relations.refresh: feeds service 21:00 UTC (python -m etl.feeds run), trailing 6 weeks; each run replaces its window, an empty pull writes nothing; a week lands about 5 days after its Saturday
relations.coverage: weeks from 2025-07-13 to the last landed week; 8 ASINs, mostly US
caveats: SUM vs MAX: total_* columns and search_query_volume are market totals repeated on every ASIN row of a query, so SUM across ASINs overstates them (5 ASIN rows = 5x): use MAX per query and period; to total OUR side SUM the asin_* columns.
Top-100 cap: Amazon reports only about the top 100 queries per ASIN and period. A query that is absent is not in that list, not zero, and a query dropping out looks like a share collapse.
Shares are percent 0-100, not fractions (2.95 = 2.95 percent).
Impressions include sponsored placements: our own ads count in asin_impressions and the shares. Purchases are search-origin and same-day and will not tie to orders.
No organic rank position exists anywhere in the data; the click, cart add and purchase shares are the proxy.
Never sum weekly rows into a month or compare a week with a month: periods overlap in meaning and the query lists differ.
Duplicate source rows (restated re-pulls) are collapsed to the latest; the newest week or month can still be partial for a week or two.

relations.name: analytics.amazon_search_queries_weekly
relations.purpose: Read the SUM-vs-MAX rule first. Amazon Brand Analytics Search Query Performance by week: for each search query and each of our ASINs, the query's market size and our share of impressions, clicks, cart adds and purchases (the organic search signal).
relations.grain: one row per (period_start = Sunday, marketplace_id, asin, query_key)
relations.refresh: feeds service 21:00 UTC (python -m etl.feeds run), trailing 6 weeks; each run replaces its window, an empty pull writes nothing; a week lands about 5 days after its Saturday
relations.coverage: weeks from 2025-07-13 to the last landed week; 8 ASINs, mostly US
caveats: SUM vs MAX: total_* columns and search_query_volume are market totals repeated on every ASIN row of a query, so SUM across ASINs overstates them (5 ASIN rows = 5x): use MAX per query and period; to total OUR side SUM the asin_* columns.
Top-100 cap: Amazon reports only about the top 100 queries per ASIN and period. A query that is absent is not in that list, not zero, and a query dropping out looks like a share collapse.
Shares are percent 0-100, not fractions (2.95 = 2.95 percent).
Impressions include sponsored placements: our own ads count in asin_impressions and the shares. Purchases are search-origin and same-day and will not tie to orders.
No organic rank position exists anywhere in the data; the click, cart add and purchase shares are the proxy.
Never sum weekly rows into a month or compare a week with a month: periods overlap in meaning and the query lists differ.
Duplicate source rows (restated re-pulls) are collapsed to the latest; the newest week or month can still be partial for a week or two.

relations.name: analytics.klaviyo_daily
relations.purpose: Klaviyo email and SMS performance by Pacific day, campaign or flow, message and channel: sends, delivered, opens, clicks, unsubscribes and Klaviyo-attributed orders and revenue.
relations.grain: one row per day (Pacific) x source ('campaign' | 'flow') x parent_id x message_id x channel (that is the primary key; message_id is '' where Klaviyo gives none)
relations.source: Klaviyo metric-aggregates (Received / Bounced / Opened / Clicked / Marked as Spam / Unsubscribed events by $flow and $message, SMS equivalents, and Placed Order - Upstackified by $attributed_flow / $attributed_message) via python -m etl.klaviyo (etl/klaviyo.py)
relations.refresh: nightly with the daily ETL; the trailing 14 complete Pacific days are replaced each run so late opens, clicks and orders land
relations.coverage: complete Pacific days through yesterday; history from the first backfill (120 days at launch)
caveats: unique_opens and unique_clicks are per-day uniques: do not add them across days or messages; sums run 20-55% above Klaviyo's single-window uniques.

orders and revenue are Klaviyo-attributed conversions of the metric 'Placed Order - Upstackified' (S6xLbC, the CheckoutChamp / Upstack server feed), dated by the day the order happened, not the day the message was sent; Shopify's own Placed Order metric reads about 10% lower.
Clicks exclude clicks Klaviyo flags as bots. sends = delivered + bounced.

Klaviyo does not expose SMS unsubscribes per flow, and campaign SMS unsubscribes are matched by campaign name with no message (message_id ''); about 2K keyword-STOP unsubscribes have no campaign and are not in this table.
SMS rows have no opens, unique_opens or spam_complaints (0).
Sends, delivered and revenue reconcile within about 3% of Klaviyo's own campaign and flow value reports.

relations.name: analytics.klaviyo_message_content
relations.purpose: The copy of every Klaviyo message (campaign message or flow message) that had activity in a pulled window, or that sits in a live flow: subject, preview text, full email HTML, readable body text and the message links. Joins to klaviyo_daily on message_id.
relations.grain: one row per message (message_id is the primary key; Klaviyo campaign message id or flow message id)
relations.source: Klaviyo API: GET /campaign-messages/{id}/template/ and /flow-messages/{id}/template/ (email HTML), the message definitions from GET /campaigns/ and /flow-actions/{id}/flow-messages/ (subject, preview, sender, SMS body), via python -m etl.klaviyo (etl/klaviyo.py)
relations.refresh: nightly with the daily ETL, for messages with activity in the trailing 14 days and every message of a live flow
relations.coverage: messages with activity in any pulled window (120 days at launch) plus live-flow messages; not every message Klaviyo has ever held
caveats: Only the latest copy is kept: when a message is edited the row is overwritten and fetched_at moves (content_hash changes); the history of edits is not kept, so old performance reads against the current copy.
Messages whose template Klaviyo no longer returns (deleted campaigns or templates) have a row with NULL html and body_text and raw.fetch_error set.

body_text is extracted from the HTML (head, scripts and styles dropped, link text kept, whitespace collapsed); image-only emails have little or no text, and image_count says how many real images the email carries. For SMS body_text is the message body and html is NULL.

relations.name: analytics.shopify_orders
relations.purpose: Order-level Shopify orders of the last 120 days (rolling), one row per order, with money, status, source, discount codes and ship-to country / region. The place to answer order-level questions (refunds, rebills, gifts, discounts) that the daily roll-ups hide.
relations.grain: one row per Shopify order (order_id is the primary key)
relations.source: ExpandFi warehouse, merchant 1452, table shopify_orders (read-only), loaded by python -m etl.shopify_orders (etl/shopify_orders.py); fields come from the order's raw Shopify JSON
relations.refresh: nightly (feeds service 21:00 UTC): the trailing 14 days are re-pulled every run, the whole 120 days every Sunday (Pacific) and on the first load; orders older than 120 days are deleted
relations.coverage: orders processed in the last 120 Pacific days, including today so far; the warehouse trails Shopify by minutes to hours
caveats: No personal data is stored: no email, name, address or phone. customer_id is the Shopify customer id (NULL when the order has none); the ship-to is country and region only.
order_date is the Pacific day of processed_at. The warehouse's own created_at is the sync time of a September backfill and is NOT used.

is_new_customer = this is the customer's first Shopify order EVER (customer key = Shopify customer id, else the lower-cased email, as in the new-customer revenue feed), judged over the whole warehouse history, not only the 120 days.

refunded_amount = total_price - current_total_price (never below 0): Shopify's current total already nets refunds and order edits, and the warehouse's refund transactions are empty for many refunds. It is a net-down amount, not a refund ledger.
Orders restated after they fall out of the trailing 14 days are picked up by the Sunday full 120-day pull, so a late refund can lag up to a week.

is_rebill = source_name is subscription_contract_checkout_one. is_trybe_gift = the order carries the tag trybe (the $0 gift orders). Gift, test and cancelled orders are kept and flagged, never dropped; filter on the flags.
Revenue by product is NOT the sum of total_price by product: use shopify_order_lines.line_net for a split.

columns.description: Pacific calendar day of processed_at; the day to group by.

columns.description: Order total after refunds and edits, as Shopify reports it now.

columns.name: refunded_amount
columns.description: total_price minus current_total_price, never below 0 (see the caveat).

columns.name: financial_status
columns.description: Shopify financial status (paid, refunded, partially_refunded, voided, ...).

columns.description: Shopify source name (web, subscription_contract_checkout_one for rebills, tiktok, or an app id).

relations.name: public.shopify_orders
relations.purpose: Order-level Shopify orders of the last 120 days (rolling), one row per order, with money, status, source, discount codes and ship-to country / region. The place to answer order-level questions (refunds, rebills, gifts, discounts) that the daily roll-ups hide.
relations.grain: one row per Shopify order (order_id is the primary key)
relations.source: ExpandFi warehouse, merchant 1452, table shopify_orders (read-only), loaded by python -m etl.shopify_orders (etl/shopify_orders.py); fields come from the order's raw Shopify JSON
relations.refresh: nightly (feeds service 21:00 UTC): the trailing 14 days are re-pulled every run, the whole 120 days every Sunday (Pacific) and on the first load; orders older than 120 days are deleted
relations.coverage: orders processed in the last 120 Pacific days, including today so far; the warehouse trails Shopify by minutes to hours
caveats: No personal data is stored: no email, name, address or phone. customer_id is the Shopify customer id (NULL when the order has none); the ship-to is country and region only.
order_date is the Pacific day of processed_at. The warehouse's own created_at is the sync time of a September backfill and is NOT used.

is_new_customer = this is the customer's first Shopify order EVER (customer key = Shopify customer id, else the lower-cased email, as in the new-customer revenue feed), judged over the whole warehouse history, not only the 120 days.

refunded_amount = total_price - current_total_price (never below 0): Shopify's current total already nets refunds and order edits, and the warehouse's refund transactions are empty for many refunds. It is a net-down amount, not a refund ledger.
Orders restated after they fall out of the trailing 14 days are picked up by the Sunday full 120-day pull, so a late refund can lag up to a week.

is_rebill = source_name is subscription_contract_checkout_one. is_trybe_gift = the order carries the tag trybe (the $0 gift orders). Gift, test and cancelled orders are kept and flagged, never dropped; filter on the flags.
Revenue by product is NOT the sum of total_price by product: use shopify_order_lines.line_net for a split.

columns.description: Human-readable order number as the store shows it.

columns.description: When the order was processed (UTC instant).

columns.description: Pacific calendar day of processed_at; the day to group by.

columns.name: customer_id

columns.name: current_total_price
columns.description: Order total after refunds and edits, as Shopify reports it now.

columns.name: refunded_amount
columns.description: total_price minus current_total_price, never below 0 (see the caveat).

columns.name: financial_status
columns.description: Shopify financial status (paid, refunded, partially_refunded, voided, ...).

columns.name: source_name
columns.description: Shopify source name (web, subscription_contract_checkout_one for rebills, tiktok, or an app id).

columns.name: app_id
columns.description: Shopify app id that created the order; NULL when none.

columns.description: Order tags, comma separated, as Shopify stores them.

columns.description: Discount codes used, comma separated; NULL when none.

columns.description: When the order was cancelled; NULL when it was not.

columns.description: True for a Shopify test order.

columns.name: is_rebill
columns.description: True for a subscription rebill (source_name subscription_contract_checkout_one).

columns.description: True when the order has the tag trybe (free sample / gift orders).

relations.name: public.klaviyo_daily
relations.purpose: Klaviyo email and SMS performance by Pacific day, campaign or flow, message and channel: sends, delivered, opens, clicks, unsubscribes and Klaviyo-attributed orders and revenue.
relations.grain: one row per day (Pacific) x source ('campaign' | 'flow') x parent_id x message_id x channel (that is the primary key; message_id is '' where Klaviyo gives none)
relations.source: Klaviyo metric-aggregates (Received / Bounced / Opened / Clicked / Marked as Spam / Unsubscribed events by $flow and $message, SMS equivalents, and Placed Order - Upstackified by $attributed_flow / $attributed_message) via python -m etl.klaviyo (etl/klaviyo.py)
relations.refresh: nightly with the daily ETL; the trailing 14 complete Pacific days are replaced each run so late opens, clicks and orders land
relations.coverage: complete Pacific days through yesterday; history from the first backfill (120 days at launch)
caveats: unique_opens and unique_clicks are per-day uniques: do not add them across days or messages; sums run 20-55% above Klaviyo's single-window uniques.

orders and revenue are Klaviyo-attributed conversions of the metric 'Placed Order - Upstackified' (S6xLbC, the CheckoutChamp / Upstack server feed), dated by the day the order happened, not the day the message was sent; Shopify's own Placed Order metric reads about 10% lower.
Clicks exclude clicks Klaviyo flags as bots. sends = delivered + bounced.

Klaviyo does not expose SMS unsubscribes per flow, and campaign SMS unsubscribes are matched by campaign name with no message (message_id ''); about 2K keyword-STOP unsubscribes have no campaign and are not in this table.
SMS rows have no opens, unique_opens or spam_complaints (0).
Sends, delivered and revenue reconcile within about 3% of Klaviyo's own campaign and flow value reports.

columns.name: parent_id

columns.name: message_id
columns.description: Klaviyo message id (campaign message or flow message); '' when the row has none (SMS unsubscribes by campaign name).

columns.name: parent_name

columns.name: sends
columns.description: Messages Klaviyo tried to send that day (delivered plus bounced).

columns.name: bounced
columns.description: Emails bounced or SMS that failed to deliver.

columns.name: opens
columns.description: Email opens (includes Apple Mail Privacy Protection machine opens); 0 for SMS.

columns.name: unique_opens
columns.description: Distinct recipients who opened that day (per-day unique, not additive); 0 for SMS.

columns.name: unique_clicks
columns.description: Distinct recipients who clicked that day (per-day unique, not additive).

columns.name: unsubscribes
columns.description: Unsubscribes counted that day (email: clicked-to-unsubscribe events; SMS: campaign-level only).

columns.name: spam_complaints
columns.description: Emails marked as spam; 0 for SMS.

columns.name: orders
columns.description: Orders Klaviyo attributes to the message, dated by order day.

columns.name: revenue
columns.description: Revenue of those orders in dollars (Placed Order - Upstackified value), dated by order day.

columns.name: loaded_at
columns.description: When this row was last written.

relations.name: public.klaviyo_message_content
relations.purpose: The copy of every Klaviyo message (campaign message or flow message) that had activity in a pulled window, or that sits in a live flow: subject, preview text, full email HTML, readable body text and the message links. Joins to klaviyo_daily on message_id.
relations.grain: one row per message (message_id is the primary key; Klaviyo campaign message id or flow message id)
relations.source: Klaviyo API: GET /campaign-messages/{id}/template/ and /flow-messages/{id}/template/ (email HTML), the message definitions from GET /campaigns/ and /flow-actions/{id}/flow-messages/ (subject, preview, sender, SMS body), via python -m etl.klaviyo (etl/klaviyo.py)
relations.refresh: nightly with the daily ETL, for messages with activity in the trailing 14 days and every message of a live flow
relations.coverage: messages with activity in any pulled window (120 days at launch) plus live-flow messages; not every message Klaviyo has ever held
caveats: Only the latest copy is kept: when a message is edited the row is overwritten and fetched_at moves (content_hash changes); the history of edits is not kept, so old performance reads against the current copy.
Messages whose template Klaviyo no longer returns (deleted campaigns or templates) have a row with NULL html and body_text and raw.fetch_error set.

body_text is extracted from the HTML (head, scripts and styles dropped, link text kept, whitespace collapsed); image-only emails have little or no text, and image_count says how many real images the email carries. For SMS body_text is the message body and html is NULL.
image_count excludes tracking pixels and 1-pixel images.

columns.name: parent_id

columns.name: body_text

columns.name: link_urls

columns.name: content_hash
columns.description: sha256 of the HTML (email) or body (SMS); changes when the message is edited.

columns.name: fetched_at

columns.name: raw

relations.name: public.klaviyo_message_performance
relations.purpose: One row per Klaviyo message with its copy (subject, preview text, body text) and its totals and rates over everything in klaviyo_daily: the table to read which copy earns.
relations.grain: one row per message_id (campaign or flow message with at least one klaviyo_daily row)
relations.source: klaviyo_daily (grouped by message_id) joined to klaviyo_message_content
relations.refresh: live (a view over klaviyo_daily; moves with the nightly Klaviyo load)
relations.coverage: the days loaded in klaviyo_daily (120 days at launch, then trailing); first_send_day is the first loaded day with sends, not the message's real first send
caveats: unique_opens_daily_sum and unique_clicks_daily_sum are sums of per-day uniques, not window uniques: a person who opens on two days counts twice. open_rate_daily_uniques and click_rate_daily_uniques are built on them and read a little high; use them to compare messages, not as Klaviyo's reported rates.
Orders and revenue are Klaviyo-attributed conversions of 'Placed Order - Upstackified', dated by the order day, so a message can show revenue with no sends when it sent before the loaded window.
Rates are NULL when delivered is 0. SMS messages have no opens. Messages without fetched copy have NULL subject / body_text and has_copy false.
SMS campaign unsubscribes are matched to the campaign, not the message, so they are not in this view.

columns.name: subject
columns.description: Email subject (current copy); NULL for SMS or when not fetched.

columns.name: unique_opens_daily_sum
columns.description: Sum of per-day unique opens (not a window unique).

columns.name: unique_clicks_daily_sum
columns.description: Sum of per-day unique clicks (not a window unique).

columns.name: revenue

columns.name: open_rate_daily_uniques

columns.name: click_rate_daily_uniques
columns.description: unique_clicks_daily_sum / delivered; NULL when delivered is 0.

columns.name: orders_per_delivered
columns.description: orders / delivered; NULL when delivered is 0.

columns.name: revenue_per_delivered
columns.description: revenue / delivered in dollars; NULL when delivered is 0.

columns.name: has_copy
columns.description: True when body_text was fetched for the message.

relations.name: public.landing_pages

relations.refresh: each run of python -m etl.landing_pages (not scheduled yet; see docs/LANDING_PAGES.md)
relations.coverage: pages of ads that had spend in the window of the first run onward

current_version_id points at the newest landing_page_versions row whose copy matches the last read (the copy can go back to an older version if the page is changed back).

columns.name: first_seen_at

columns.name: active

relations.name: public.landing_page_versions
relations.purpose: The copy of a landing page as it was on a given read: title, description, ordered text blocks with heading level, buttons, prices, guarantee sentences, review snippets and image alt text.
relations.grain: one row per (landing page, content hash): a new row exists only when the copy changed (id is the primary key)
relations.source: etl/landing_pages.py: a plain public web request per page, parsed with the standard library (headless Chromium for pages built in the browser)
relations.refresh: each run of python -m etl.landing_pages; a row is added only when the text hash changes
relations.coverage: from the first read of each page
caveats: content_hash covers the text only (title, description, text blocks, button text, image alt text), not image addresses or scripts, so changing a picture without changing its alt text is not a new version.
Pages built in the browser have little text in the server HTML; those are read again with Chromium and rendered_in_browser is true. Text shown only after a click or inside an iframe is not captured.
fetched_at is when this exact copy was first seen, not when it was last confirmed (landing_pages.last_fetched_at has that).

columns.name: landing_page_id
columns.description: Page this copy belongs to (landing_pages.id, foreign key).

columns.name: content_hash
columns.description: sha256 of the page text (see caveats); unique per page.

columns.name: fetched_at
columns.description: When this copy was first seen.

columns.name: http_status
columns.description: HTTP status of the read that produced this copy.

columns.name: title

columns.name: meta_description
columns.description: Meta description (else the Open Graph description).

columns.name: rendered_in_browser
columns.description: True when the copy came from headless Chromium because the server HTML held almost no text.

columns.name: blocks
columns.description: Ordered text blocks as JSON: [{i, tag, level, text}], level is the heading level 1 to 6 or null, tag is the nearest label tag (h1..h6, p, li, blockquote, button, a, text).

columns.name: ctas
columns.description: Button and call to action text as JSON: [{text, href, tag}].

columns.name: prices
columns.description: Dollar amounts found in the text as JSON: [{price, context}].

columns.name: guarantees
columns.description: Sentences that mention a guarantee, refund, money back or risk free, as a JSON array of strings.

columns.name: reviews

columns.name: images
columns.description: Image alt text as JSON: [{alt, src}].

columns.name: full_text
columns.description: All text blocks joined by new lines, for searching.

relations.name: public.landing_page_ads
relations.purpose: Which Meta ad sends people to which landing page, and how that link was found.
relations.grain: one row per (ad, landing page) (ad_id + landing_page_id is the primary key)
relations.source: etl/landing_pages.py: the Meta ad creative, the Page post an ad reuses, or the ad preview
relations.refresh: each run of python -m etl.landing_pages (new ads with spend only; --refresh-ads looks at all again)
relations.coverage: ads with spend in the 30 days before each run, from the first run onward
caveats: An ad whose creative lists several links has one row per page. Its spend counts in full under each page in landing_page_top_ads, so spend must not be added across pages.
ad_id is not a foreign key to meta_ads because ads can be deleted in Meta.

columns.name: raw_url
columns.description: The link exactly as Meta returned it (with tracking parameters).

columns.name: source
columns.description: How the link was found: 'creative' (the ad's own creative), 'post' (the Page post the ad reuses), or 'preview' (the ad preview).

columns.name: first_seen_date
columns.description: Date the ad was first found with this link.

columns.name: last_seen_date
columns.description: Date the link was last confirmed.

relations.name: public.landing_page_ad_checks
relations.purpose: Ads that etl/landing_pages.py has already looked at, so an ad with no readable link is not asked about every night.
relations.grain: one row per ad (ad_id is the primary key)
relations.coverage: ads with spend in the window of the runs
caveats: An ad with result no_link or error is looked at again 14 days after checked_at.

columns.name: checked_at
columns.description: When the ad was last looked at.

columns.name: result
