relations.name: public.landing_page_top_ads
relations.purpose: The ads that drive each landing page, ranked by spend over the last 7 and the last 30 days, with Meta-reported purchases, revenue and ROAS (revenue divided by spend).
relations.grain: one row per (landing page, window_days, ad): window_days is 7 or 30; only ads with spend in the window appear
relations.refresh: live view; the ad to page map moves with each run of python -m etl.landing_pages, spend with the nightly Meta pull
relations.coverage: ads mapped to a page by the landing page job
caveats: Purchases and revenue are what Meta reports (all customers), not Upstack new-customer numbers; join analytics.meta_ad_daily on ad_id when you need those.
An ad that lists several links appears under each page with its full spend: do not add spend across pages.
The window is the last N Pacific calendar days including today, which is a partial day.

columns.name: ad_name
columns.description: Ad name from meta_ads; NULL when the ad is not there.

columns.name: campaign_id
columns.description: Campaign id from meta_ads; NULL when the ad is not there.

columns.name: revenue
columns.description: Meta-reported purchase revenue in the window, dollars.

columns.name: rank_by_spend
columns.description: 1 = biggest spender for this page and window.

relations.name: public.brain_keys
relations.purpose: Agent keys for the hosted brain endpoint (/mcp). With sign-in on: one row per user who made a key on the Connect an agent page (a reset replaces it). With the app open (AUTH_DISABLED): one row per key anyone made, with no user. A brain key opens /mcp and nothing else.
relations.grain: one row per key (id is the primary key; key_hash is unique; username is unique and NULL for open-app keys)
relations.source: the Connect an agent page (POST /api/brain/key in app/brain_mcp.py); last_used_at is touched by /mcp
relations.refresh: on demand (a person makes a key; last_used_at moves at most once a minute while the key is in use)
relations.coverage: from the day migration 220 was deployed; open-app keys from migration 221
caveats: Only the sha256 hash of the key is stored. The key is shown once and cannot be recovered; a signed-in user resets it to get a new one (the old one stops working at once). Open-app keys cannot be reset, only made again.
Separate from api_keys: a brain key never works on any /api/ route, and an api_keys key also works on /mcp.
Open-app keys (created_by = 'open-app') are capped at 50 per day for the whole app and keep only a salted hash of the creator's IP, never the IP.

columns.name: username
columns.description: App login of the owner (a name from APP_USERS), unique: one key per user. NULL for open-app keys.

columns.name: key_hash
columns.description: sha256 hex digest of the full key (unique); the key is looked up by this hash.

columns.name: prefix
columns.description: First 8 characters of the key ('lvb_' plus 4), for display only.

columns.name: created_at
columns.description: When the key was made or last reset.

columns.name: last_used_at
columns.description: When the key last made a /mcp request (at most once a minute); NULL while unused.

columns.name: created_by
columns.description: How the key was made: 'signed-in' (a logged-in user, username is set) or 'open-app' (made while AUTH_DISABLED was on, username is NULL).

columns.name: creator_hash
columns.description: For open-app keys: HMAC-SHA256 of the creator's IP address under the app's secret key (first 32 hex characters); never the IP itself. NULL for signed-in keys.

relations.name: public.brain_audit
relations.purpose: Audit log of the hosted brain endpoint: one row per tool call (who, which tool, how long, how many rows). Never holds the question, the SQL or the result.

relations.coverage: from the day migration 220 was deployed; no pruning

row_count is NULL for tools that return no row list (describe, app_map).

columns.name: actor

columns.name: tool

columns.name: duration_ms

columns.name: ok

excluded.name: public.schema_migrations
excluded.reason: Migration runner bookkeeping (version, applied_at). Infrastructure, no business data.

excluded.name: public.feed_oauth
excluded.reason: Holds the encrypted ExpandFi OAuth refresh token (a credential). Never documented column by column and never exposed.

metrics.name: spend
metrics.label: Ad spend
metrics.formula: sum(spend) over the days. Total spend = Meta spend + Google spend; a ratio's spend is always the sum over the same days and rows as its numerator.
metrics.default_basis: Meta (Graph API, both ad accounts) + Google Ads, platform-reported dollars: the 'Total spend' of the Marketing metrics app (app/trends.py build_catalog(), total_spend).
other_bases: Meta spend alone (the product bands' Total column divides by it)
Business-wide spend in pacing = Meta + Google + TikTok and other platforms + Amazon ads (app/projection/pacing/catalog.py, biz_total_spend)
analytics.platform_daily_history.spend for days before 2026-05-06 (Meta ad level starts 2026-05-06; campaign grain from 2024-12-31 in analytics.meta_campaign_daily_history)
traps: Spend adds across platforms; purchases and revenue never do.
Meta days are each ad account's own day (Main = Los Angeles, BackUp = New York); Google, Upstack and orders are Pacific days.
The last 3-7 days still move (Meta restates), and today is never loaded.

metrics.name: meta_purchases
metrics.label: Meta-reported purchases
metrics.formula: sum(meta_purchases): purchases Meta reports for the ad that day (omni_purchase, else purchase, else pixel purchase), Meta's default attribution.
metrics.default_basis: Meta-reported (counts returning customers, Meta's attribution window)
other_bases: Upstack new customers (analytics.meta_ad_daily.upstack_new_customers): first orders only
Upstack all orders (upstack_orders): every order Upstack credits
traps: Never compare Upstack new customers with Meta's all purchases: Meta counts returning customers, Upstack's new-customer basis does not (they are different quantities, not one number measured twice).
Meta and Google credit the same orders: never add Meta purchases to Google's.
Meta counts a returning customer's order as a purchase; it is not a new customer.

metrics.name: landing_page_views
metrics.label: Meta landing page views
metrics.formula: sum(landing_page_views): landing page views Meta reports for the ad that day (omni_landing_page_view, else landing_page_view): clicks where the page actually loaded.
metrics.default_basis: Meta-reported (default attribution), all ad accounts
other_bases: Link clicks (analytics.meta_ad_daily.link_clicks): clicks before the page loads, always at least as large
Unique outbound clicks (analytics.meta_reach / meta_product_reach): de-duplicated per person, a different denominator
traps: NULL (not 0) on days before the 2026-11-12 funnel backfill: sum only over rows where it is not NULL, and divide by the matching rows' other columns.
LPV / link clicks is typically 70-95%: a lower share means slow pages or lost clicks, not fewer buyers.
Not comparable to Upstack site visitors (analytics.site_traffic_daily): different tracker.

metrics.name: add_to_carts
metrics.label: Meta adds to cart
metrics.formula: sum(add_to_carts): adds to cart Meta reports for the ad that day (omni_add_to_cart, else add_to_cart, else pixel add to cart), the 'Adds to cart' of Ads Manager.
metrics.default_basis: Meta-reported (default attribution, includes returning customers)
other_bases: Meta purchases (analytics.meta_ad_daily.meta_purchases)
traps: NULL (not 0) on days before the 2026-11-12 funnel backfill.

The funnel rates are ratios of sums over the same ad-days and rows: link click to add to cart = sum(add_to_carts) / sum(link_clicks); landing page view to add to cart = sum(add_to_carts) / sum(landing_page_views); add to cart to purchase = sum(meta_purchases) / sum(add_to_carts). Never average per-ad rates.
Purchases count returning customers, so add to cart to purchase is a Meta-attribution rate, not a new-customer conversion rate.

metrics.name: initiated_checkouts
metrics.label: Meta initiated checkouts
metrics.formula: sum(initiated_checkouts): checkouts Meta reports initiated for the ad that day (omni_initiated_checkout, else initiate_checkout, else pixel initiate checkout), the 'Checkouts initiated' of Ads Manager.
metrics.default_basis: Meta-reported (default attribution, includes returning customers)
other_bases: Meta purchases (analytics.meta_ad_daily.meta_purchases)
Upstack orders (analytics.meta_ad_daily.upstack_orders): another tracker
traps: NULL (not 0) on days before the checkout backfill: sum only over rows where it is not NULL, and divide only by sums over the same rows.

Funnel rates are ratios of sums over the same ad-days: add to cart to initiated checkout = sum(initiated_checkouts) / sum(add_to_carts); initiated checkout to purchase = sum(meta_purchases) / sum(initiated_checkouts); payment info to purchase = sum(meta_purchases) / sum(payment_info_adds). Never average per-ad rates.

Purchases count returning customers, so initiated checkout to purchase is a Meta-attribution rate, not a new-customer conversion rate. Checkout events fire on the pixel: a checkout that never loads the pixel (an in-app browser that blocks it) is not counted, so a fall in initiated checkouts is not proof of fewer checkouts.

metrics.name: payment_info_adds
metrics.label: Meta payment info added
metrics.formula: sum(payment_info_adds): payment-info-added events Meta reports for the ad that day (omni_add_payment_info, else add_payment_info, else pixel add payment info), the step between initiated checkout and purchase.
metrics.default_basis: Meta-reported (default attribution, includes returning customers)
other_bases: Initiated checkouts (analytics.meta_ad_daily.initiated_checkouts)
Meta purchases (analytics.meta_ad_daily.meta_purchases)
traps: NULL (not 0) on days before the checkout backfill.

It can exceed initiated checkouts on a day (a customer re-entering payment details, or express wallets that skip the initiate event): use it as a trend, not as a stage that must be smaller than the one before.
Same attribution as purchases, so it counts returning customers.

metrics.name: atc_to_ic_rate
metrics.label: Add to cart to initiated checkout rate
metrics.formula: sum(initiated_checkouts) / sum(add_to_carts): the share of adds to cart that go on to start checkout, as a ratio of sums over the same ad-days (Meta-reported).
metrics.default_basis: Meta-reported (default attribution, includes returning customers)
other_bases: Link click to add to cart and landing page view to add to cart (see add_to_carts)
traps: Restrict to rows where both columns are not NULL; never average per-ad rates.
Not a new-customer rate: Meta counts returning customers in both counts.

metrics.name: ic_to_purchase_rate
metrics.label: Initiated checkout to purchase rate
metrics.formula: sum(meta_purchases) / sum(initiated_checkouts): the share of started checkouts that Meta credits with a purchase, as a ratio of sums over the same ad-days (Meta-reported).
metrics.default_basis: Meta-reported (default attribution, includes returning customers)
other_bases: Upstack new-customer orders per initiated checkout (upstack_new_customers / initiated_checkouts) mixes bases: say so if used
Add to cart to purchase (see add_to_carts)
traps: Restrict to rows where initiated_checkouts is not NULL; never average per-ad rates.
Purchases use Meta's attribution window and can land on a later day than the checkout, so a single day's rate is noisy and the last days still move.

metrics.name: meta_change_log
metrics.label: Meta change log (budget, bid, status, targeting changes)
metrics.formula: count of rows in analytics.meta_change_log by event_type and event_day; budget and bid amounts in old_amount / new_amount (dollars). Ad set settings by day: analytics.meta_adset_state_daily; their day-over-day differences: analytics.meta_change_ledger.
metrics.default_basis: Meta activity log (read only), both ad accounts
other_bases: Ad set snapshot differences (analytics.meta_change_ledger), from its first snapshot day: independent of the log's extra_data
traps: A change is not a cause: say 'a bid change on N ad sets preceded the move', never 'the bid change caused it', unless a control supports it.
The log's extra_data is often incomplete for bids and caps; cross-check with analytics.meta_change_ledger, which only exists from its first snapshot day.
System events (first_delivery_event, Pending Review flips, billing, image adds) dominate the row count: filter to the event types you mean.
Campaign budget (CBO) changes are update_campaign_budget with object_level campaign; ad set budgets are update_ad_set_budget with object_level adset.

metrics.name: meta_roas
metrics.label: Meta ROAS (platform ROAS)
metrics.formula: sum(meta_revenue) / sum(spend): Meta-reported purchase value over spend, as a ratio of sums.
metrics.default_basis: Meta-reported purchase value / Meta spend
other_bases: Upstack new-customer ROAS (upstack_nc_roas)
Upstack all-orders ROAS (upstack_all_orders_roas)
Total NC ROAS (total_nc_roas): actual new-customer revenue over total spend
traps: Never average daily ROAS: divide the sums.
Meta ROAS counts returning customers and runs well above Total NC ROAS: they answer different questions.

Creative-level ROAS in analytics.creative_family_metrics / priorities_concepts is the same Meta-reported ratio but over each ad's life since launch (blank under $100 spend in the priorities snapshot).

metrics.name: meta_cpa
metrics.label: Meta cost per purchase
metrics.formula: sum(spend) / sum(meta_purchases).
metrics.default_basis: Meta-reported purchases
other_bases: Upstack new-customer CPA over Meta spend (spend / upstack_new_customers)
Total NC CPA (nc_cpa): total spend / actual new customers
traps: Never compare Upstack new customers with Meta's all purchases: Meta counts returning customers, Upstack's new-customer basis does not (they are different quantities, not one number measured twice).
This is not the NC CPA the business quotes (that one divides by actual new customers, see nc_cpa).

metrics.name: upstack_new_customers
metrics.label: Upstack-attributed new customers
metrics.formula: sum(upstack_new_customers): first-time customers Upstack credits to the ad under any-click, 30-day attribution (utm_source 'Meta Ads').
metrics.default_basis: Upstack new customers (first orders only, any-click 30-day, Pacific days)
other_bases: Upstack all orders (upstack_orders): every order credited, returning included
Last-click by source (analytics.attribution_source_daily): exclusive per order, a different basis
traps: NULL, not 0, on days Upstack was not pulled (Meta before 2026-05-06, Google before 2025-05-13).

Any-click credits an ad on days it spent nothing (spend = 0, upstack_* > 0 is normal); one customer can be credited to several ads, so sums over ads of different families can exceed orders_daily.new_customers.
About 1.3% of credited orders match no Meta ad (analytics.attribution_unmapped_daily): in orders_daily, in no ad row.
Never compare Upstack new customers with Meta's all purchases: Meta counts returning customers, Upstack's new-customer basis does not (they are different quantities, not one number measured twice).

metrics.name: upstack_nc_roas
metrics.label: Upstack new-customer ROAS (attributed)
metrics.formula: sum(upstack_new_customer_revenue) / sum(spend) over the rows where Upstack was pulled (upstack_new_customers IS NOT NULL).
metrics.default_basis: Upstack new customers (the default basis everywhere in the Marketing metrics app: 'Count: New customers')
other_bases: Upstack all orders (upstack_all_orders_roas)
Meta-reported (meta_roas)
traps: Never compare Upstack new customers with Meta's all purchases: Meta counts returning customers, Upstack's new-customer basis does not (they are different quantities, not one number measured twice).
Restrict spend to days Upstack covers or the ratio is diluted by uncovered days.
When one ad is copied into several ad sets under one name, Upstack's credit is split by Meta spend that day: family and higher sums are exact, one copy's own numbers are an allocation.
Attribution, not the actual: the business's real new-customer revenue is orders_daily (see nc_revenue / total_nc_roas).

metrics.name: upstack_all_orders_roas
metrics.label: Upstack all-orders ROAS (attributed)
metrics.formula: sum(upstack_order_revenue) / sum(spend) over the rows where Upstack was pulled.
metrics.default_basis: Upstack all orders (every order Upstack credits to the ad, any-click 30 days)
other_bases: Upstack new customers (upstack_nc_roas): the default basis
Meta-reported (meta_roas)
traps: Use this only against Meta's all-purchases basis, never against upstack_nc_roas.
Includes returning customers' orders, so it flatters acquisition efficiency; the Marketing metrics app shows it only when 'Count: All orders' is chosen.

metrics.name: nc_revenue
metrics.label: New-customer revenue (actual)
metrics.formula: sum(new_customer_revenue): first-order revenue per Pacific day, counted once (Upstack order-level measures).
metrics.default_basis: Actual orders feed (analytics.orders_daily), gross: tax included, before refunds
other_bases: By product (analytics.orders_by_product_daily): order total split across product lines by net line price
Attributed to Meta or Google (upstack_new_customer_revenue): an attribution, not the actual
traps: Not the sum of platform columns: platforms overlap, this is counted once.
A day with no orders is absent from orders_daily, not 0.
Revenue is gross of tax and refunds (the Marketing metrics app describes it as 'tax included, before refunds'); net = total_revenue - tax - refunds in analytics.orders_daily_detail.
The trailing 7 days are restated nightly.

metrics.name: nc_orders
metrics.label: New customers (actual)
metrics.formula: sum(new_customers): customers whose first Shopify order fell on the day, counted once.
metrics.default_basis: Actual orders feed (analytics.orders_daily)
other_bases: By product (orders whose largest product line is the product)
Upstack-attributed new customers (upstack_new_customers)
traps: Not additive with attributed new customers: those credit the same customer to several ads or platforms.
Customers, not orders: a first order is the unit.

metrics.name: total_nc_roas
metrics.label: Total NC ROAS
metrics.formula: sum(orders_daily.new_customer_revenue) / (sum(Meta spend) + sum(Google spend)) over the days that Meta, Google and orders_daily all cover, as a ratio of sums.
metrics.default_basis: Actual new-customer revenue / Meta + Google spend (app/trends.py build_catalog(), nc_roas)
other_bases: NC ROAS on Meta spend alone (meta_nc_roas in app/trends.py build_catalog()): the product bands' Total column
Business-wide NC ROAS in pacing = (Shopify + Amazon new-customer revenue) / (Meta + Google + TikTok + other + Amazon ads) (app/projection/pacing/catalog.py, biz_nc_roas)
Per-product NC ROAS = analytics.orders_by_product_daily revenue / analytics.meta_product_daily spend
traps: The numerator is actual revenue counted once, not the sum of the platforms' purchase values.
Use only days all three sources cover and compute the ratio of sums, never an average of daily ratios.
Gross revenue (tax included, before refunds); the deal's net-of-tax goal basis is lower.
Amazon is not in this ratio (the Marketing metrics app's total covers Shopify, Meta and Google).

metrics.name: nc_cpa
metrics.label: NC CPA (cost per new customer)
metrics.formula: (sum(Meta spend) + sum(Google spend)) / sum(orders_daily.new_customers), over the days all three sources cover.
metrics.default_basis: Total spend / actual new customers (app/trends.py build_catalog(), nc_cpa)
other_bases: Meta spend / actual new customers (meta_nc_cpa): the product bands' Total column
Testing / scaling NC CPA = stage spend / any-click new customers of that stage (analytics.attribution_anyclick_daily)
Upstack-attributed NC CPA = spend / upstack_new_customers (a different, attributed basis)
traps: Divides by ACTUAL new customers, not by attributed ones or by Meta purchases.
Per-product NC CPA counts new customers whose largest product line is the product (analytics.orders_by_product_daily).

metrics.name: mer
metrics.label: MER (marketing efficiency ratio)
metrics.formula: sum(total_revenue) / (sum(Meta spend) + sum(Google spend)) over the days all three sources cover.
metrics.default_basis: Orders feed total revenue (no Amazon) / Meta + Google spend (app/trends.py build_catalog(), mer)
other_bases: Business-wide MER in pacing adds Amazon revenue and Amazon / TikTok / other spend (app/projection/pacing/catalog.py, biz_mer)
traps: Total revenue here is gross (tax included, before refunds) and has no Amazon revenue; the matching spend has no Amazon or TikTok spend.

metrics.name: conversion_rate_uoc
metrics.label: Conversion rate on unique outbound clicks
metrics.formula: actual new customers / Meta unique outbound clicks: per product = orders_by_product_daily.new_customers / meta_product_reach.unique_outbound_clicks; total = orders_daily.new_customers / meta_reach.unique_outbound_clicks.
metrics.default_basis: Actual new customers / unique outbound clicks (app/projection/pacing/catalog.py, meta_cvr_<product> and prod_cvr_total; every click-based pacing metric uses UNIQUE OUTBOUND clicks)
other_bases: Meta CVR = Meta purchases / Meta link clicks (meta_cvr)
NC conversion (clicks) = new customers / (Meta link clicks + Google clicks) (app/trends.py build_catalog(), nc_cvr_clicks)
NC conversion (visitors) = new customers / Upstack new visitors (analytics.site_traffic_daily): the Marketing metrics app's nc_cvr
traps: Unique outbound clicks exist only from 2026-07-05 (Meta serves filtered unique clicks ~120 days back); earlier periods are blank, not 0.
Unique clicks are not additive: read the row of the period's own grain (day, week or month) in meta_reach / meta_product_reach.
The three products' unique clicks add to 1.01-1.06x the account-level figure, so the product rates do not average to the total.
Meta's total link_click count (analytics.meta_ad_daily.link_clicks) is a different, larger denominator than unique outbound clicks: do not mix the two.

metrics.name: cpm
metrics.label: CPM (cost per 1,000 impressions)
metrics.formula: sum(spend) / sum(impressions) x 1000.
metrics.default_basis: Meta spend / Meta impressions x 1000 (app/trends.py build_catalog(), m_cpm)
other_bases: Pacing divides spend by the account-level impressions pulled at the period's own grain (app/projection/pacing/catalog.py, meta_cpm)
Cost per 1,000 reached = spend / reach x 1000 (a different, higher number)
traps: Impressions add across days, reach does not: for CPM either source works, for frequency only meta_reach.
Meta days are the ad account's own day.

metrics.name: frequency
metrics.label: Frequency
metrics.formula: impressions / reach, both taken at the SAME grain (a day's, a week's or a month's own row): analytics.meta_reach.frequency.
metrics.default_basis: Account level, both ad accounts, at the grain you read (app/projection/pacing/catalog.py, meta_frequency)
other_bases: No frequency exists per ad, ad set, campaign or product (reach is account level only)
traps: Reach is de-duplicated by Meta and NOT additive: never average daily frequencies or sum daily reach to get a week or month; use the week / month rows.
The current day, week and month are partial.
Frequency here is the same-day overlap between ad sets, not exposure on more days.

metrics.name: hit_rate
metrics.label: Creative hit rate
metrics.formula: Display hit rate = ads whose since-launch spend reached $10,000 / launched ads (first tracker rows of an ad family with a launch date or any spend). Scoring hit rate = mature (>= 14 days old) judged ads (>= $100 spent) that reached $1,000 / mature judged ads, shrunk toward the product average.
metrics.default_basis: Display: $10,000 since-launch spend over launched ads, Meta basis (etl/creative_priorities.py TOP_SPEND = 10000; the definition of a hit since 2026-11-10, docs/CREATIVE_PRIORITIES.md)
other_bases: Scoring: HIT_SPEND = $1,000 over mature judged ads (priorities_concepts.hit_rate, hit_rate_index): the stored hit_rate in the snapshot and in the CSV export's hit_rate / hit_rate_index columns
Hits out of tested ads: $10,000 / ads that spent $100 or more (hit_rate_10k_of_tested)
traps: A KNOWN SPLIT: the displayed hit rate uses $10,000, but the priorities CSV export's hit_rate and hit_rate_index columns (and the score's hit-rate component) still use $1,000 (etl/creative_priorities.py: HIT_SPEND vs TOP_SPEND; docs/CREATIVE_PRIORITIES.md). Name which one you quote.
Launched counts every launched ad including recent ones with $0 spend; new ads need time to reach $10,000, so young cohorts read low.
Metrics sit on the FIRST tracker row of each ad family: filter is_first_row.

metrics.name: test_to_scale_rate
metrics.label: Test-to-scale rate (% reached scaling)
metrics.formula: creatives that moved / creatives that began in testing, among creatives launched in the window and not launched before the data starts: count(*) FILTER (WHERE moved) / count(*) WHERE began_in_testing AND NOT launched_before_data_start AND first_day in window.
metrics.default_basis: Meta basis (analytics.creative_stage_moves.basis = 'meta'); the basis changes only the money columns, never who moved (app/promotions.py _cohorts / build)
other_bases: upstack_new_customers and upstack_all_orders: same creatives and moves, Upstack purchases and revenue
traps: A creative MOVED only when it spent in a Testing campaign and first spent in a Scaling campaign on a LATER day (a campaign is Testing when its name contains 'test').
Hide bulk days: 40 or more creatives entering scaling on one day (moves_that_day >= 40) is a mass relaunch, not a set of test winners.
Creatives that launched straight into scaling are not testers and never in the rate; a new creative needs time to move (analytics.creative_stage_moves.days_in_test): recent cohorts read low.
'Held up' = (scale_revenue / scale_spend) / (test_revenue / test_spend): held >= 0.90, softer >= 0.70, fell below; too early before $200 and 3 days in scaling.

metrics.name: repeat_revenue
metrics.label: Repeat revenue
metrics.formula: Modeled: sum over cohorts of first-order revenue x curve[age] in the month at that age (age 0 = the acquisition month has no repeat): max(0, new_customers x first_order_per_customer x curve[age]) (app/projection/cohorts/engine.py repeat_for).
metrics.default_basis: Modeled from the cohort table and the chosen retention curve (Live or Goal; scenario lever cohorts.curve_source in analytics.projection_levers)
other_bases: Actual returning revenue = analytics.orders_daily.returning_customer_revenue (Upstack, gross)
Business-wide repeat = Shopify returning revenue + Amazon revenue not from new customers (app/projection/pacing/catalog.py, biz_repeat_rev)
Historical months come from the books (analytics.projection_actuals 'pnl.repeat_rev'); the model only projects forward
traps: Repeat revenue is a projection driven by the curve choice; always say which curve (Live last N cohorts, Goal snapshot, as-of month).
The cohort table must hold only CLOSED months: a cell that lands in a month that is not over is blanked.
Gross of tax and refunds, like all pacing revenue.

metrics.name: retention_curve
metrics.label: Retention curve (Live vs Goal)
metrics.formula: Repeat dollars per $1 of first-order revenue by age (months after acquisition). Live at age a = weighted average (weights new customers) of increment / first_order over the newest N cohorts that have a non-blank, non-zero increment at that age (usable_rank <= N); from age 28 on = previous age x 0.95. Goal = the newest saved snapshot of analytics.cohorts_curve_goal.
metrics.default_basis: Live curve over the last 3 cohorts (app/projection/cohorts/engine.py Levers.n_cohorts = 3, tail_decay 0.95, tail_from_age 28)
other_bases: Live over the last 6 cohorts (the P&L page offers 3 or 6; the deal notes mention 6; scenario lever cohorts.n_cohorts)
Goal curve (analytics.cohorts_curve_goal, is_active)
As-of curve: the Live curve re-derived from what was observable at the end of a past month
Blend: w x Goal + (1 - w) x Live
traps: Say Live or Goal and N: the lifetime sums differ (compare sum(value) of the Goal curve with the Live curve you compute).
Never include a month that is not over; cohort exports differ by source (Shopify cohort dollars vs Upstack's), so do not mix sources between refreshes.
Ages beyond 36 are the tail formula, not data.

metrics.name: payback
metrics.label: Payback (months)
metrics.formula: First age (months after the first order, 0 = the first order pays) where cumulative contribution per new customer >= CAC. Inputs (aov, cac, product_cost_pct, fulfillment, max_age, curve) = analytics.projection_levers where module = 'financing' and lever = 'payback' (a json object holding only what the scenario sets; unset keys take the code defaults in app/projection/financing/params.py: product_cost_pct 0.1726, fulfillment 5.53, max_age 36, curve 'live'; aov and cac default to None = not typed). Contribution of the first order cm = AOV x (1 - product cost %) - fulfillment per order; month k adds cm x curve[k]; cumulative = cm + sum cm x curve.
metrics.default_basis: Product margin: cost per order = product cost % x AOV + fulfillment (app/projection/financing/calc.py payback(); the quick hint app/projection/drivers/payback.py is the same arithmetic)
other_bases: Fully loaded ('all variable costs'): cost per order = loaded_rate x AOV with the P&L's own product, fulfillment, shipping, payment and chargeback rates (fully_loaded=True)
Interpolated months (months_interpolated) between the last unpaid and the first paid age
cohorts_monthly.payback_months: the payback exported with each cohort (a different, historical measure)
traps: Payback on product margin is much shorter than fully loaded: always name the basis.
The curve behind it (Live N cohorts vs Goal) moves the answer by a month at some scales.
Contribution, not revenue: do not compare cumulative revenue with CAC.

metrics.name: gross_vs_net_revenue
metrics.label: Gross vs net revenue (pacing is gross)
metrics.formula: Gross = total_revenue (tax included, before refunds). Net = total_revenue - tax - refunds. Plan basis = total_revenue - the plan's sales-tax estimate (+ Amazon).
metrics.default_basis: Gross: the pacing page, the P&L and every ROAS / MER here are gross; refunds are a memo row only (decision 2026-11-04)
other_bases: Net of tax and refunds (app/projection/pacing/catalog.py, biz_total_rev_net)
Plan basis: Shopify total less the sales-tax estimate, plus Amazon: the basis of the P&L revenue goal (biz_total_rev_plan)
traps: The monthly plan block and Month Snapshot compare against the P&L goal, which is net of the estimated sales tax (docs/projection/MODULE_pacing.md): comparing gross Shopify revenue with that goal overstates pacing.

Refunds are not deducted anywhere unless you subtract them (net = gross - tax - refunds): refunds were 11% of DTC revenue in Nov 1-2, so a net-of-refunds basis paced about 101% of goal, not 106% (docs/projection/MODULE_pacing.md, open items).

metrics.name: sales_tax_deduction
metrics.label: Sales-tax deduction (estimate)
metrics.formula: Sales tax(m) = 0 for a month whose DTC revenue is loaded from the books (already net of tax), else -(sales_tax_rate x DTC revenue(m)); sales_tax_rate = analytics.projection_levers where module = 'drivers' and lever = 'sales_tax_rate'; no row means the code default 0.07. It reduces total revenue.
metrics.default_basis: Estimate: 7% of DTC revenue for months not yet closed in the books (app/projection/drivers/revenue.py, drivers/model.py DEFAULT_SALES_TAX)
other_bases: Actual tax collected (analytics.orders_daily_detail.tax), used by pacing's net view
Closed books months carry no deduction
traps: Open question (docs/projection/SKEPTIC_REPORT.md, SHEET_FINDINGS.md S1): the deduction applies from Jul-26 while history months carry none and the DTC revenue behind it is already net of tax; removing it adds about $535K to FY27 NOI. Settle against the Aug QuickBooks close or set drivers.sales_tax_rate to 0.
DTC rows of the pacing page stay gross on purpose; only the goal / projection total is net of the estimate.

metrics.name: repeat_share
metrics.label: Repeat share of revenue
metrics.formula: sum(returning_customer_revenue) / sum(total_revenue).
metrics.default_basis: Actual orders feed, Shopify only (app/trends.py build_catalog(), repeat_share)
other_bases: Business-wide: (Shopify returning + Amazon non-new-customer revenue) / (Shopify + Amazon revenue) (app/projection/pacing/catalog.py, biz_repeat_share)
traps: Gross of tax and refunds; no Amazon in the Shopify-only ratio.

metrics.name: daily_story_baseline
metrics.label: Same-weekday baseline (daily story)
metrics.formula: For a target day D: the same weekday in the previous four weeks (D-7, D-14, D-21, D-28; fewer when history is short). Tables show the median of those days' own values and the pooled value (sum / sum); the decomposition uses the pooled value.
metrics.default_basis: median of the up to four same-weekday days for the metric table; pooled for the exact decomposition
other_bases: trailing 7 days before D, pooled (metrics.<key>.trailing_7d)
traps: A same-weekday baseline removes the weekday pattern only; it does not hold changes (new ad sets, bids, sends) constant, so it is not a like-for-like control for any one cause.
Early days (May 2026) have fewer than four baseline weeks.

metrics.name: daily_story_noise_z
metrics.label: Noise range and z-score (daily story)
metrics.formula: noise = sample standard deviation of the previous 28 days of the same daily metric; z = (value on D - same-weekday median baseline) / noise; a metric is flagged when |z| >= 2. Needs at least 10 trailing days.
metrics.default_basis: daily values of the metric on the same basis as the value (ratios from each day's sums)
other_bases: Facts path: metrics.<key>.z, noise_std_28d and flag inside the JSON
traps: A daily ratio's noise is large (NC ROAS moves several tenths day to day), so most days are inside it.
z compares one day with a baseline; it does not say why the day moved.

metrics.name: daily_story_decomposition
metrics.label: Exact decomposition of NC ROAS (daily story)
metrics.formula: NC ROAS = AOV x (Meta spend / total spend) x (1000 / CPM) x CTR x (link click to landing page view) x (view to add to cart) x (add to cart to new customer) [x add to cart to initiated checkout, initiated checkout to new customer when the column exists]. The log change against the pooled same-weekday baseline splits exactly into one contribution per term; percentage points are the total percentage move split in proportion to each term's log.
metrics.default_basis: headline NC ROAS: orders_daily new-customer revenue / (Meta + Google spend); the funnel terms use Meta link clicks, landing page views and adds to cart over all actual new customers
other_bases: ad-attributed NC ROAS (a cut for ads, products, structures): sum(upstack_new_customer_revenue) / Meta spend
traps: Arithmetic, not cause: it says which term moved, not why.
add to cart to new customer divides all actual new customers (including non-Meta ones) by Meta adds to cart, so it is a ratio of the day's totals, not Meta's own conversion.

metrics.name: daily_story_mix_rate
metrics.label: Mix versus rate (daily story)
metrics.formula: Over segments (product, stage, campaign structure, market cluster, ICP, format, vendor, age, ad family): ROAS = sum(w_i r_i) with w_i the segment's share of spend and r_i its ad-attributed NC ROAS. mix_i = (w_i - w0_i) x (rbar_i - Rbar), rate_i = (r_i - r0_i) x wbar_i, where 0 is the pooled same-weekday baseline and bars are the mean of day and baseline; sum(mix_i + rate_i) equals the total move exactly.
metrics.default_basis: ad-attributed NC ROAS (Upstack any-click 30-day attribution of new customers to Meta ads), a cut only
other_bases: Facts path: cuts.<cut>.mix_rate, cuts.<cut>.rows[].effect and movers inside the JSON
traps: Mix = spend moving between segments with different returns; rate = the same segment earning more or less per dollar. Neither is a cause.
Ad-attributed revenue is any-click and is not the headline: it does not add up to orders_daily new-customer revenue.

metrics.name: daily_story_pattern_lift
metrics.label: Pattern lift (daily story scoreboard)
metrics.formula: For a change type: rise_rate = days whose next 1-3 days averaged more than 5% above the same-weekday baseline / days with that change; rise_lift = rise_rate - base_rise_rate (the same rate over all days). fall_lift likewise.
metrics.default_basis: Upstack new-customer basis for NC ROAS and AOV; Meta-reported for CPM and CTR; conversion = actual new customers / Meta link clicks
other_bases: The base rate (all days) sits in the same row as base_rise_rate and base_fall_rate
traps: Correlation, not cause: changes land together and the 1-3 day outcome windows of neighbouring days overlap.
Only rows with n of 6 or more are listed; a high rate on a small n is not evidence.
